- **No speedup:** It reproduces the same algorithm/distribution with comparable polynomial resources; quantum hardware
  supplies randomness but no improved asymptotic complexity.
- **Subtlety:** A BPP machine may use polynomially many random bits in general; the exercise specifies \(\log n\), fine.
- **Circuit conversion:** Reversible implementation/garbage adds overhead not discussed in the expected one sentence.

#### Chapter 33 opening — claimed nonclassical tasks

  quantum communication; classical channels can transmit classical descriptions for known states. State the resource
  separation precisely.
- **QKD:** Classical information-theoretically secure key agreement is impossible under comparable unauthenticated/
  no-pre-shared-secret assumptions, but QKD still requires authenticated classical communication.

#### Chapter 33 opening — loss/infrastructure thesis

- **Fiber loss:** \(0.2\,\mathrm{dB/km}\) near 1550 nm is standard modern telecom-fiber attenuation; wavelength,
  connectors, splices, and detector efficiency add loss. Replace `\\,`.
- **Satellite sentence:** Quantum memory in LEO is not normally the primary limitation for satellite trusted-node QKD;
  many links do not store quantum states on the satellite. Visibility, diffraction, pointing, atmosphere, daylight, and
  trust are the main issues. This is a conceptual error.
- **No-cloning/amplification:** Correct: unknown quantum states cannot be noiselessly copied/amplified. Quantum-limited
  amplifiers exist but add noise and do not restore lost qubits.
- **Repeater list:** Twin-field QKD and satellites can extend key distribution without general stored-entanglement
  networking; not every item is an answer via distributing entanglement.
- **Core loss thesis:** Excellent.

#### §33.1 — resource-accounting setup

- **Resource inequalities:** Teleportation and dense coding are better expressed as asymptotic resource inequalities,
  e.g. \(2[c\!\to\!c]+[qq]\succeq[q\!\to\!q]\) and
  \([q\!\to\!q]+[qq]\succeq2[c\!\to\!c]\), to avoid saying literal resource conversion without direction/availability.
- **“Bidirectional”:** The two protocols are related but not simple inverses under identical resources.
- **Qubit channel:** A use of an ideal noiseless quantum channel versus physically sending a carrier should be
  distinguished.
- **Ebit:** Definition is good.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Bookkeeping lens is valuable.

#### §33.1 — teleportation identity

- **Identity check:** With Bell states
  \(|\Psi^-\rangle=(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)/\sqrt2\), the Bob state for the \(\Psi^-\) branch is typically
  \(\alpha|1\rangle-\beta|0\rangle\), as written, up to convention/global sign. Verify all branches and correction map.
- **Corrections:** For standard Bell-bit labeling, corrections may be \(I,Z,X,XZ\) up to phases/order. State mapping
  explicitly rather than an unordered set.
- **Destruction:** Alice’s input state is consumed; her measured physical qubits remain classical/post-measurement.
- **Exactness:** Holds for ideal Bell pair, gates, measurement, and classical communication; real fidelity is limited by
  entanglement/noise.
- **No qubit traveled:** Misleading literally: the pre-shared ebit had to be distributed by quantum communication or
  physical transport earlier. No carrier bearing the unknown state travels *during the teleportation step*.
- **Classical information:** The two measurement bits are uniformly random and reveal nothing about \(|\psi\rangle\);
  worth adding.
- **Escaping:** Many doubled LaTeX escapes (`\\,`, `\\{...\}`) need cleanup.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** The explicit identity is satisfying.

#### §33.1 — superdense coding

- **Mapping:** \(Z^{b_1}X^{b_2}\) maps \(\Phi^+\) to Bell states up to a global phase; provide bit-to-state table to avoid
  convention ambiguity.
- **Capacity wording:** Entanglement-assisted classical capacity of a noiseless qubit channel is two classical bits per
  qubit sent when one ebit is consumed. An “unaided qubit channel” has one classical bit per use for orthogonal encoding
  by Holevo.
- **“Twice Holevo capacity”:** The Holevo theorem/bound also applies in entanglement-assisted settings with a different
  ensemble/resource formulation; phrase “twice the unassisted classical capacity.”
- **Prior entanglement distribution:** Its cost is excluded from the one-use accounting and must be counted end-to-end.
- **Cross-reference:** Verify §12.5.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Clean dual to teleportation.

#### §33.1 — conversion table/generalization

- **No-signaling:** Correct.
- **“Neither beats Holevo”:** Dense coding changes the entanglement-assisted channel capacity; it does not violate
  Holevo. Teleportation is not chiefly a classical-capacity protocol.
- **Universal generalization false:** QKD, repeaters, and blind computation cannot all be reduced to bookkeeping only
  among ideal qubit channels, cbits, and ebits; privacy, authentication, noisy channels, secret bits, quantum memories,
  trust, and computation are additional resources.
- **Rate budget:** Practical rates also depend on loss, fidelity, memory lifetime, multiplexing, detector dark counts,
  finite-key security, and classical latency.
- **Recommendation:** Keep table, limit the claim to entanglement-assisted communication primitives.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Elegant but overunified.

#### §33.1 — teleportation as network workhorse

- **Relativity/no-cloning:** Correct.
- **“Decouple legs”:** Pre-shared entanglement turns later quantum-state transmission into two classical bits, but only
  while adequate high-fidelity ebits remain.
- **Accumulated pool:** Quantum memories decohere; generation is stochastic; purification/error correction consumes
  pairs. “When conditions favorable” is plausible but must include storage lifetime.
- **Logical qubit:** Teleporting an encoded logical state may require encoded Bell pairs, transversal logical Bell
  measurement, or code conversion—not simply one physical ebit.
- **“Every architecture”:** Direct trusted-node QKD, prepare-and-measure networks, and satellite downlinks may target key
  delivery rather than generic entanglement distribution. Avoid universal.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Strong explanation of why entanglement generation precedes networking.

#### §33.2 — QKD/security setup

- **One-time pad:** Perfect secrecy requires uniformly random key at least as long as the message, used once, and secure
  authentication/integrity separately.
- **Authentication bootstrap:** QKD requires an authenticated classical channel, normally bootstrapped from a small
  pre-shared key or public-key authentication. It expands keys; it does not solve authentication from nothing.
- **Security wording:** “Guaranteed by laws of physics” is marketing-like. Composable security depends on device models,
  implementations, randomness, finite statistics, authenticated classical processing, and proof assumptions.
- **Cross-reference:** Verify Chapter 27 and avoid duplication.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Clear motivation.

#### §33.2 — BB84 preparation/sifting

- **Source realism:** Original ideal BB84 uses single photons; deployed decoy-state BB84 uses phase-randomized weak
  coherent pulses. The section later corrects this, but flag idealization immediately.
- **State escaping:** Replace `\\{...\}`.
- **Basis probabilities:** Efficient BB84 often uses biased basis choices rather than uniform 50/50 to reduce sifting
  loss.
- **Public channel:** Must be authenticated, though not secret.
- **QBER sampling:** Finite-key random sampling bounds phase errors; it is more than comparing a sacrificed subset
  informally.
- **Error correction leakage:** Privacy amplification accounts for revealed syndrome information and Eve’s bound.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Classic protocol remains very readable.

#### §33.2 — BB84 threshold/eavesdropper explanation

- **11% scope:** About 11% is the asymptotic one-way secret-key threshold for ideal single-photon BB84 under standard
  proofs/collective attacks; thresholds depend on reconciliation, proof, finite size, devices, and preprocessing.
- **Intercept-resend:** Wrong-basis measurement produces 25% QBER on sifted bits under ideal full intercept-resend, but
  security proofs cover coherent attacks; the paragraph should not imply all Eve can do is measure each photon.
- **“Any eavesdropper … must guess”:** False. Eve may use quantum memories, coherent interactions, side channels, photon-
  number attacks, detector blinding, or collective measurements. The no-information-without-disturbance intuition is
  fine but this is too narrow.
- **Threshold action:** Below threshold does not automatically make a positive key rate; observed statistics, losses,
  error correction efficiency, finite-key size, and device parameters matter.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Strong intuitive story needing modern-security caveat.

#### §33.2 — E91/device independence

- **Bell state choice:** Original E91 uses singlet entanglement; using \(\Phi^+\) is conventionally equivalent with
  adjusted settings but should not be presented as historical exactness.
- **Basis count/protocol:** Verify original measurement choices and which rounds form key/test.
- **Self-testing claim:** A maximal/near-maximal CHSH violation self-tests state and measurements jointly up to local
  isometries/junk under noncommunication assumptions; it does not merely certify the source and then measurements.
- **Intercept-resend:** Bell violation supports secrecy via monogamy/randomness, not just foreclosing one attack.
- **Device-independent assumptions:** Requires trusted labs, random choices, no unwanted leakage, authenticated classical
  channel, isolation/no communication, and detection efficiency; it is not assumption-free.
- **Locality:** QKD devices need isolation during rounds; space-like separation is one way, with protocol-specific
  requirements.
- **Field status:** Fully DIQKD has experimental demonstrations but very low rates/distances; verify current 2026 record.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Deep and compelling.

#### §33.2 — B92

- **Measurement description likely wrong:** Standard B92 receiver uses measurements capable of conclusively ruling out
  one of two nonorthogonal states; unambiguous state discrimination is a related framing, but a single POVM can identify
  states with inconclusive outcomes. Specify exact POVM/basis implementation.
- **Security:** Loss opens vulnerabilities and security thresholds/implementations are subtler than a simple
  interception story.
- **“Simpler”:** Two-state preparation is simpler, but receiver/security/efficiency tradeoffs matter.
- **Wastefulness:** Quantify conclusive probability, which depends on overlap.
- **Modern relevance:** Explain why B92 is included versus MDI-QKD/CV-QKD.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Nice minimalist contrast.

#### §33.2 — decoy-state QKD

- **Phase randomization:** Weak coherent pulses must be phase randomized for the Poisson photon-number mixture used in
  standard decoy proofs.
- **PNS wording:** Eve can in an idealized attack keep one photon and forward the rest, exploiting channel loss; she
  cannot necessarily “siphon” without constraints in an implementation-independent description.
- **Key mechanism:** Decoy intensities let parties estimate yields/error rates conditional on photon number because Eve
  cannot condition on the *intensity label* beyond photon number. Saying attack affects all intensities “equally” is
  imprecise; yields for the same \(n\)-photon component should be intensity-independent.
- **Attributions:** Verify Hwang/Lo–Ma–Chen/Wang author/year results. “Lo et al.” should be bibliographically exact.
- **Every deployed system:** Unsupported universal; likely most modern weak-coherent BB84 systems use decoys, but
  entangled/single-photon/CV implementations differ.
- **“Closes loophole”:** Under source assumptions/proof; implementation side channels remain.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Excellent example of protocol engineering defeating a concrete attack.

#### §33.2 — PLOB theorem/equation

- **Theorem scope:** PLOB gives the two-way assisted secret-key capacity of a pure-loss bosonic channel,
  \(-\log_2(1-\eta)\), per channel use, allowing unlimited two-way classical communication and no repeaters.
- **Small-\(\eta\) approximation:** \(R\approx\eta/\ln2\), so stated orders should include the factor 1.44.
- **Fiber conversion:** \(0.2\) dB/km yields \(\eta=10^{-0.02L}=10^{-L/50}\), correct; replace `\\,`.
- **200 km value:** \(\eta=10^{-4}\), PLOB ≈\(1.44\times10^{-4}\), order \(10^{-4}\), correct.
- **500 km value:** \(\eta=10^{-10}\), PLOB ≈\(1.44\times10^{-10}\), correct.
- **Device losses:** Detector/coupling loss can be folded into effective transmittance, reducing practical rate.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** One equation explains the entire distance problem.

#### §33.2 — claimed ways around PLOB

- **“Hard ceiling”:** Correct for repeaterless point-to-point pure-loss channel under theorem assumptions, not every
  physical direct link with side channels/multimode accounting.
- **Trusted nodes:** Classical trusted relays can extend QKD distance without entanglement repeaters but change trust
  model; missing from list despite deployed networks relying on them.
- **Satellite:** A satellite link changes loss geometry/channel segmentation, but trusted satellite QKD may still use
  direct channels on each pass.
- **Twin-field:** It beats the repeaterless linear-in-\(\eta\) rate-loss scaling with \(\sqrt\eta\)-like behavior using an
  untrusted middle measurement, without being a general quantum repeater. “Breaks direct-channel assumption” is useful
  but needs care around network/channel uses and security proof.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Strong transition.

#### §33.2 — deployed BB84 claims

- **Vendor list:** Current products/company status and protocol variants for ID Quantique, Toshiba, QuantumCTek, KEEQuant
  require primary dated sources.
- **Clock versus key rate:** GHz pulse clock does not imply GHz detection/key. Secret rates vary by distance, detector,
  loss, finite-key block, duty cycle, and reconciliation.
- **Range/rate envelope:** kbit/s–Mbit/s over 50–100 km is too broad to be meaningful and may overstate simultaneous
  performance at 100 km. Provide a table of specific field trials.
- **“Dark fiber”:** Correct distinction; deployed systems may use wavelength multiplexing on lit fiber with coexistence
  penalties too.
- **Backbone production:** Beijing–Shanghai uses trusted relay nodes and may combine protocols; EuroQCI is an initiative/
  pilots rather than one production network; US testbeds vary. Verify “all run decoy BB84” and production status.
- **Security/economics conclusion:** Excellent—compare QKD’s physical assumptions, trusted hardware/nodes, cost and
  denial-of-service behavior with PQC’s scalable software deployment.
- **Cross-reference:** Verify §27.4.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Concrete and decision-relevant.

#### §33.3 — fiber-loss calculation

- **Formula:** At 0.2 dB/km, \(\eta=10^{-0.02L}\); at 100 km, \(\eta=10^{-2}=1\%\), correct.
- **Wavelength:** 1550 nm is in a low-loss telecom window, though not literally a unique absorption minimum and installed
  link loss includes splices/connectors/bends/detectors.
- **Escaping:** Replace all `\\,`.
- **Amplification:** No-cloning blocks noiseless regeneration of an arbitrary qubit, but trusted measure-and-prepare nodes
  can relay classical keys; distinguish them from quantum repeaters.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** A crisp quantitative antagonist.

#### §33.3 — entanglement swapping

- **Mechanism:** Correct ideal Bell-measurement description; endpoint state is known up to an outcome-dependent Pauli
  frame, so classical outcome communication/correction is required.
- **“No quantum information traversing full path”:** Each elementary Bell pair required quantum transmission over its
  link; no single carrier traverses end-to-end.
- **Bell measurement:** Linear optics cannot deterministically distinguish all four photonic Bell states without extra
  resources; practical success probability matters.
- **Arbitrary hops:** Fidelity, swap success, memory lifetime, classical latency, and nested scheduling make iteration
  nontrivial.
- **Figure:** Inspect SVG labels, accessibility, correction messages, memories, and whether two intermediate nodes match
  prose.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** The central network primitive is explained clearly.

#### §33.3 — repeater probability/scaling

- **Naïve \(p^n\):** Simultaneous independent success gives \(p^n\); direct transmission versus segmented link probability
  and attempt synchronization should be defined.
- **Polynomial claim:** Memory-assisted nested repeaters can change rate-loss scaling under idealized fixed per-link
  parameters, but finite memory, swap probability, purification and decreasing segment length complicate a blanket
  polynomial-in-\(n\) statement.
- **Coherence requirement:** Must exceed stochastic waiting plus classical communication, local operations, nesting, and
  purification—not merely “network delay.”
- **Multiplexing:** Temporal/spectral/spatial multiplexing is a central way to improve rate and should be introduced.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Excellent reason for quantum memory.

#### §33.3 — DLCZ

- **Platform history:** Original DLCZ uses atomic ensembles and linear optics; rare-earth crystals and NV centers are
  related repeater platforms but not simply newer versions of the same ensemble/cavity implementation.
- **Excitation regime:** Weak Raman write pulses must suppress double excitations; a Stokes click heralds a collective
  spin wave, with vacuum/multiphoton components affecting fidelity.
- **Midpoint click:** Single-photon interference erases which-path information and heralds ensemble entanglement; calling
  this a “swap of the photonic mode” is imprecise.
- **Cavity:** Original proposal does not require every ensemble to be cavity coupled; check.
- **Read process:** Anti-Stokes retrieval efficiency, phase stability, indistinguishability, detector dark counts and
  memory decoherence dominate.
- **“Every subsequent”:** Overstatement; all-photonic/error-corrected repeaters can depart from the memory-herald-swap
  template.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Rich physical mechanism.

#### §33.3 — purification/distillation

- **Input count:** Recurrence protocols use two or more noisy pairs plus bilateral operations/classical comparison;
  success/fidelity depends on Bell-diagonal form/threshold and local noise.
- **\(F'>F\):** Not automatic for arbitrary states/fidelities/noisy gates; there is a distillability/threshold condition.
- **Yield wording:** Repeated recurrence reduces yield exponentially in number of rounds, but hashing/breeding protocols
  can have nonzero asymptotic yield above thresholds. Do not characterize all distillation this way.
- **Attribution:** Verify full author lists/acronyms (BBPSSW, DEJMPS) and dates.
- **Scheduling:** Correct and practically important; include multiplexing and age-dependent fidelity.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** The distance-versus-purity tradeoff is compelling.

#### §33.3 — repeater-generation attribution/taxonomy

- **Historical error:** Briegel et al. 1998 introduced quantum repeaters, not the later “first-generation
  classification.” Muralidharan et al. developed a three-generation taxonomy. Rewrite attribution.
- **Taxonomy variability:** Other reviews use first/second/third generation differently; cite and define once.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Useful organizing scheme after attribution repair.

#### §33.3 — first-generation repeaters

- **Description:** Heralding, memories, swapping, purification, and two-way signaling broadly fit the taxonomy.
- **Rate:** Polynomial claim needs ideal assumptions; round-trip latency is one limiter among probabilistic generation,
  memory efficiency/lifetime, local gates, detector rates, and nesting.
- **“All current demonstrations”:** All-photonic repeater experiments and error-detection demonstrations may not fit;
  avoid universal.
- **DLCZ inclusion:** Correct broad family.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Clear.

#### §33.3 — second-generation repeaters

- **Taxonomy likely inaccurate:** In common three-generation taxonomy, second generation uses heralded entanglement
  generation to handle loss and QEC for operation errors; it still needs two-way signaling for loss/heralding, not
  necessarily “for the swap.”
- **“Deterministic QEC”:** Syndrome extraction/correction can be deterministic at logical level but requires fault-
  tolerant gates/ancillas and may fail logically.
- **Examples:** Surface-code patches are large, not “small block codes”; avoid grouping them.
- **Critical path:** Heralding latency remains.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Good conceptual middle tier with technical repair needed.

#### §33.3 — third-generation repeaters

- **Description:** One-way QEC corrects both loss and operation errors, avoiding round-trip signaling in the standard
  taxonomy; broad idea correct.
- **Carrier wording:** “Logical photon” is misleading; encoded photonic blocks distribute a logical qubit across multiple
  photons/modes.
- **Code examples:** Cat and GKP are bosonic oscillator codes not straightforward “multi-photon codes” in the same sense
  as parity codes; verify suitability in cited repeater proposals.
- **Local processing:** Stations still need measurement/feed-forward and classical processing, just not end-to-end
  acknowledgment before forwarding.
- **Classical-amplifier analogy:** No-cloning still applies; rate-loss scaling may become favorable with dense stations/
  high overhead, not literal amplification.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Strong futuristic contrast.

#### §33.3 — current laboratory status

- **Highly volatile:** Every institution, distance, year, memory time, and “no deployed node” claim needs exact 2026
  primary/independent verification.
- **Delft:** Verify whether 2021–2024 NV networking distances were tens of meters/campus fiber rather than “several
  kilometers.” This may be materially wrong.
- **Ion links:** Innsbruck/Oxford platform, distance, fiber/free-space wording, and node architecture may be conflated.
- **Rare-earth memories:** Geneva/Caltech attribution and “approaching 1 s” are likely outdated/underspecified; coherence
  time, storage efficiency, bandwidth, on-demand retrieval, and entanglement preservation differ.
- **“Solidly first generation”:** Some record components are not integrated repeaters at all; component milestone is not
  a repeater-generation demonstration.
- **Wild deployment:** Metropolitan test networks have elementary entanglement links/nodes; define deployed repeater
  function carefully.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Concrete status is valuable if rigorously sourced.

#### §33.3 — memoryless versus memory-assisted

- **Terminology:** A node performing swapping with no storage may be a relay/measurement station; “memoryless quantum
  repeater” also refers to all-photonic repeater schemes that use photonic cluster states and feed-forward without long-
  lived matter memories. The paragraph’s definition is too narrow.
- **Simultaneity:** Multiplexing/photonic graph states can avoid a simple all-links-simultaneous \(p^n\) penalty.
- **False universal:** DLCZ is not “and all subsequent designs”; third-generation and all-photonic proposals differ.
- **MDI:** Standard MDI-QKD has an untrusted middle Bell measurement, not a multihop swap chain.
- **Memory metrics:** Coherence, efficiency and multimode capacity are central; add fidelity, wavelength/interface,
  bandwidth, on-demand retrieval, initialization, and local-gate performance.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Important distinction, outdated taxonomy.

#### §33.4 — satellite-link physics/loss

- **Atmosphere wording:** Most atmospheric mass lies in the lowest ~10–15 km, but turbulence, clouds, aerosols and
  absorption affect slant paths; “vacuum essentially loss-free” still leaves diffraction/geometric spreading.
- **Loss budget:** 10–30 dB for a 500 km downlink is geometry/weather/aperture/wavelength dependent and likely optimistic
  at the low end. Cite an actual link budget including detector/coupling losses.
- **Fiber comparison:** 300 km ×0.2 dB/km =60 dB fiber attenuation, so the broad contrast is sound.
- **1550 nm:** Micius and many free-space demonstrations use wavelengths near 800–850 nm rather than telecom 1550 nm;
  do not imply one universal satellite wavelength.
- **Uplink/downlink:** Downlinks generally suffer less turbulence-induced beam spreading than uplinks; mention.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Orbit bypassing fiber is a powerful architectural insight.

#### §33.4 — Micius history/demonstrations

- **Protocol attribution:** Verify whether Micius decoy-state QKD downlinks, trusted-relay Beijing–Vienna key exchange,
  entanglement distribution, and entanglement-based QKD occurred in the stated years/stations.
- **Trusted satellite:** The Beijing–Vienna link relied on the satellite as a trusted relay, with keys established on
  separate passes and combined; it was not end-to-end quantum entanglement over 7600 km.
- **Videoconference:** Demonstration used keys refreshed through the satellite/backbone, while ordinary encrypted video
  traffic remained classical; say so.
- **1200 km:** Ground-station separation/link geometry and Bell-test/entanglement rate need exact source.
- **E91 wording:** Verify whether the satellite experiment is formally E91 QKD or entanglement-based QKD/BBM92.
- **Operational:** “Operational since 2017” needs current mission status; satellites age.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Landmark experiments deserve this level of detail.

#### §33.4 — 2026 satellite mission/status claims

- **Extremely volatile:** Browse primary agency/mission sources before publication. Launch schedules commonly slip, and
  “followed” falsely implies all listed missions have flown.
- **SpeQtre/SpeQtral-1:** Verify naming, operator, launch/status, and whether these are separate satellites/mission

- **QEYSSat/EAGLE-1/QUBE-II/CAPSat:** Verify launch dates/current status/objectives; future missions must not be described
  as completed commercial followers.
- **“First non-experimental services”:** Strong market claim requiring named provider, customer, operational start,

- **Customer claim:** Government/finance targeting is not evidence of service delivery.
- **Constellations:** “Funded but not yet flying” may already be stale or contradicted by Chinese constellation plans/
  launches; exact date essential.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Useful status snapshot, high risk of rapid obsolescence.

#### §33.4 — twin-field QKD protocol

- **Attribution:** Verify Lucamarini–Yuan–Dynes–Shields 2018 paper/title and distinguish original TF-QKD from later
  phase-matching/sending-or-not-sending variants with complete security proofs.
- **“MDI variant of BB84”:** Broad family relation is defensible but original TF-QKD is not simply BB84; phase encoding,
  phase announcement/slicing, decoys and security details matter.
- **Phase randomization tension:** Users need phase coherence/reference between independent lasers while global phases
  may be randomized/announced in bins; simple “phase-randomized pulses encoding key in phase” hides the core technical
  challenge.
- **Relay:** Single-photon interference at a beamsplitter, not a full Bell-state measurement.
- **Scaling:** Ideal TF protocols can achieve \(O(\sqrt{\eta})\) and surpass repeaterless PLOB under specified channel-use
  accounting/security assumptions.
- **“Quadratic”:** It is quadratic in exponent/transmittance relationship, not a universal factor-two speedup.
- **No repeaters:** Correct long-lived quantum memories are unnecessary.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Elegant midpoint interference story.

#### §33.4 — twin-field distance records

- **Record-list hazard:** Every 511/605/658/830/>1000 km distance, fiber type (spool versus installed), attenuation,
  secret-key rate, finite/asymptotic security, protocol variant, date, and institution must be sourced.
- **Distance versus loss:** Ultra-low-loss spools and installed field fiber at the same kilometer distance are not
  equivalent; report total dB and achieved key bits/rate.
- **Institution grouping:** Shanghai/Hefei/Toshiba/Beijing–Tianjin may conflate multiple papers/groups.
- **“Recent”:** Replace with exact date.
- **Relay security statement wrong:** MDI security does not follow because tampering “affects both arms identically.”
  The relay can behave arbitrarily; security is designed so detector outcomes reveal no key beyond bounded information.
- **Universal “only”:** TF-QKD may not be the only memoryless architecture/protocol surpassing point-to-point PLOB under
  network bounds; phase-matching/related protocols and all-photonic repeater proposals complicate the claim.
- **“Leading candidate”:** Forecast/ranking needs support.
- **BB84 collapse:** Direct rates become impractical gradually, not at a universal 300 km threshold.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** The distance race is exciting but should not become a record dump.

#### §33.4 — MDI-QKD

- **Attribution:** Lo–Curty–Qi 2012 is standard; verify title/year.
- **Protocol:** Alice/Bob send phase-randomized decoy BB84 states to an untrusted relay performing partial Bell-state
  measurement; correct high level.
- **“All detector attacks”:** MDI-QKD removes detector side channels from the trusted endpoints under source-security
  assumptions, but implementation flaws at sources/reference frames/classical systems remain. Avoid “all.”
- **Dominant attack surface:** Detector hacking has been prominent, but “dominant” requires evidence.
- **TF relationship:** TF-QKD is related to MDI ideas but uses single-photon interference and distinct security proofs;
  calling it merely a refinement can obscure foundational differences.
- **Rate:** Standard MDI-QKD generally scales with total transmittance \(\eta\); TF improves the scaling.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Helpful family context.

#### §33.5 — network/layering opening

- **Definition:** Routability, multiple users, resource scheduling, service interfaces, failure handling and layering are
  suitable distinctions from a point-to-point link.
- **Primitive:** Ebitts are one network service/resource, but QKD networks may transport weak coherent pulses and
  classical keys without stored ebits. “Primitive is the ebit rather than the bit” overgeneralizes an entanglement-
  distribution architecture to every quantum network.
- **OSI analogy:** Helpful, but quantum stacks often require cross-layer scheduling because memories decohere while
  classical stacks deliberately hide many lower-layer details.
- **Decade/history:** Quantum-network architecture work predates the last decade; say formal stacks matured recently.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Familiar network language offers a strong handhold.

#### §33.5 — Wehner–Elkouss–Hanson attribution

- **Likely factual error:** The 2018 *Science* paper “Quantum internet: A vision for the road ahead” defines six hardware/
  capability stages, not necessarily the exact four-layer stack attributed here. A later architectural paper may define
  physical/link/network/transport layers. Verify primary source and attribution.
- **“Reference architecture”:** No universally standardized quantum Internet stack exists; IETF/IRTF, ETSI, research
  projects and simulators use related but differing abstractions.
- **Four versus five:** Calling four layers the reference and then five the working framing needs a cited version/
  evolution.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Useful organization, potentially assigned to the wrong paper.

#### §33.5 — physical-layer bullet

- **Scope:** Physical layer includes photon generation/conversion, optical channel, synchronization, stabilization,
  memories, detection and control—not only heralded ebit generation.
- **Protocol list:** DLCZ is an end-to-end elementary-link protocol with memory interaction; “single-click/two-click” are
  detection schemes; photon-number resolving describes detector capability. The list mixes abstraction levels.
- **Output:** Some physical attempts output raw detection events/no ebit; successful heralding prepares an imperfect
  entangled state with metadata (fidelity/time/memory IDs).
- **Adjacent storage:** Memoryless/all-photonic links may not output a stored matter ebit.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Concrete but overfitted to one hardware family.

#### §33.5 — link-layer bullet

- **Reliability analogy:** Quantum link layers cannot simply retry invisibly: attempts consume time/memory, fidelity
  decays, and no-cloning prevents buffering/copying arbitrary payloads.
- **“Robust”:** Define service semantics—requested number/fidelity/deadline, heralded success/failure, memory ownership,
  and expiration.
- **Ethernet MAC:** Link scheduling/acknowledgment analogy is useful, but Ethernet frames and ebits have different
  persistence/error semantics.
- **Existing protocol:** Link-layer protocols such as EG/EQP should be named if this is derived from a specific stack.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Strong engineering analogy.

#### §33.5 — network-layer bullet

- **Routing objective:** Quantum routing optimizes probability, rate, fidelity, memory occupancy, age, swap success and
  classical latency—not just shortest path.
- **IP analogy:** IP forwards packets hop-by-hop; entanglement routing reserves/generates correlated link resources and
  coordinates nonlocal swaps. Explain the crucial difference.
- **Pauli frames:** Swap outcomes/metadata must reach endpoints for correction/interpretation.
- **Failure/retry:** A failed swap consumes input pairs, requiring rescheduling.
- **Multi-path:** Entanglement can be purified/combined across paths; route semantics differ from packets.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Makes the distinctive scheduling problem visible.

#### §33.5 — transport-layer bullet

- **Placement:** Purification may occur hop-by-hop, nested, or end-to-end; assigning it exclusively to transport is an
  architectural choice, not universal fact.
- **Fidelity guarantee:** Fidelity may be estimated/model-derived rather than directly known for each ebit; confidence,
  age, deadline and success probability belong in the service contract.
- **End-to-end analogy:** Strong but quantum transport cannot retransmit an unknown application state after destructive
  failure unless the application retained/re-encodes it.
- **Application examples:** QKD does not necessarily consume high-fidelity ebits, and clock synchronization may use
  multipartite states/photons rather than a generic Bell-pair API.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** The “ebit of at least F” API is memorable.

#### §33.5 — application-layer extension

- **Standardization claim:** “Most current research” needs a survey; quantum stack proposals range from three to seven
  layers and sometimes separate control/management planes.
- **Blind computing:** Requires computation service, authentication, classical interaction and trust assumptions beyond
  an application label.
- **Distributed sensing:** May require synchronized multipartite entanglement and timing services absent from simple
  Bell-pair transport.
- **Improvement:** Present this as one useful reference stack, then show variants/control plane.
- **Entertainment: 3/5.** Brief but necessary.

#### §33.5 — simulator catalog

- **Volatile inventory:** Verify current repositories/releases/licenses/maintainers and whether each tool is active as of

- **NetSquid:** Proprietary/free-for-research access and Python/discrete-event capabilities matter to readers.
- **SeQUeNCe/QuISP/SimQN:** Verify institutional attributions, abstraction, scale and supported protocols.

  role.

#### §33.5 — simulator scale/history claim

- **Arbitrary topology:** Plausible as a graph input, but simulator fidelity/performance depends on state formalism and
  entanglement size.
- **\(10^3\)-node scale:** Strong benchmark requiring exact simulator, protocol, hardware, state representation, machine
  and runtime. Multipartite quantum-state simulation does not scale merely because event scheduling does.
- **“2022-onwards”:** NetSquid (2021), QuISP and earlier network simulators existed before/around this; exact historical
  assertion likely false.
- **DLCZ-era comparison:** General discrete-event/network simulation existed; quantum-specific mature tools arrived
  gradually.
- **Recommendation:** Add a maintained comparison table rather than prose superlatives.

#### §33.5 — five network primitives

- **Generation:** Correct core service; direct photon/state transmission and QKD raw-key generation are additional
  primitives in non-ebit-centric networks.
- **Swapping:** Correct, including classical outcome/Pauli-frame metadata.
- **Distillation:** “Two into one” is a recurrence example, not universal; multi-pair/hashing/error-corrected protocols
  differ and improvement is conditional.
- **Multipartite distribution:** Arbitrary graph states are not always obtainable by a few swaps/local Cliffords from an
  arbitrary ebit layout without resource/measurement overhead; graph-state fusion rules matter.
- **State transfer:** Teleportation is common in repeater networks, but direct physical transmission and encoded
  one-way repeaters are alternatives; “almost always” lacks evidence.
- **Missing operations:** Memory allocation, frequency conversion, synchronization, purification/error correction,
  routing, verification and classical control are services/operations too.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Compact practical vocabulary.

#### §33.5 — GHZ distribution/applications

- **Conference key:** Multipartite conference key agreement can use GHZ states, but security/trust/device assumptions
  and alternatives should be noted.
- **Anonymous voting:** GHZ enables certain protocols; anonymity/fairness/authentication/collusion guarantees are model-
  dependent.
- **Sensing:** Resource-matched/noise-aware advantage required.
- **Recipe incomplete:** Starting with Bell pairs from center A to B/C, local operations and measurement can create GHZ,
  but exact CNOT direction, measured qubit, correction bits, and retained qubits must be specified.
- **“Any graph”:** Arbitrary graph-state distribution from a star does not “generalize straightforwardly” without
  significant Bell pairs, local qubits, CZ/fusion operations, classical corrections and topology-specific overhead.
- **Center trust:** Central preparation can create a trust/failure bottleneck.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Concrete multiparty extension is engaging.

#### §33.5 — star topology

- **“Direct ebits”:** A hub may have physical links/pair-generation capability, not permanently held ebits; memories
  expire.
- **Cheap leaf:** Physical fiber/free-space interface, wavelength/synchronization, memory and routing additions are not
  inherently cheap.
- **Trust:** A swapping-only untrusted hub need not learn endpoint keys/state, while a trusted QKD relay does; the bullet
  partly acknowledges this but “participates in entanglement” does not necessarily imply trust.
- **Capacity:** Hub detector/memory/interface contention is a throughput bottleneck.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Familiar topology tradeoff.

#### §33.5 — linear topology

- **Backbone reality:** Current long-haul QKD chains usually use trusted classical key relays, not quantum repeater nodes.
  Clarify.
- **Naturalness:** Geography/fiber rights-of-way favor chains, but rings/meshes provide resilience.
- **Critical path:** Correct; end-to-end success/fidelity worsens with hop count and each node.
- **Failure domains:** A compromised trusted node versus a failed untrusted repeater have different consequences.
- **Entertainment: 3/5.** Clear.

#### §33.5 — mesh topology

- **Benefits:** Multiple paths aid availability/load balancing, but quantum multipath routing cannot freely duplicate
  unknown states.
- **“Goal of any”:** Unsupported universal. Some city networks are purpose-built star/ring/tree and do not need full
  mesh.
- **Scheduling:** Memory-slot contention, link stochasticity, fidelity/age, wavelength resources and classical control
  make it difficult; good.
- **Shortest path:** More hops may be worse even if physical distance is shorter; link quality matters.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Strong distributed-systems connection.

#### §33.5 — 2026 pilot-network list

- **Primary-source audit required:** Every network’s current operational status, nodes, protocol, topology, trusted-node
  architecture, dates and users must be verified.
- **EuroQCI:** It is a multinational infrastructure program with national projects/procurement, not necessarily unified
  “pilot lines” in each named country.
- **US names:** Chicago Quantum Exchange/Argonne/Fermilab, ESnet testbeds, Brookhaven/Stony Brook and Lincoln Lab may

- **Tokyo:** Verify whether the longstanding testbed is still operational/updated in 2026.
- **Topology claim:** Mostly star/linear may be broadly true but needs network maps.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Geographic specificity is compelling if accurate.

#### §33.5 — trusted-node explanation

- **Key handling:** Trusted relays may receive hop-by-hop keys and combine/relay end-to-end keys using one-time-pad XOR,
  not necessarily decrypt and re-encrypt user data. The prose wrongly suggests payload decryption.
- **Trust cost:** Any relay compromise can expose end-to-end key material; physical security and key-management controls
  are central.
- **Physical-security phrase:** QKD retains link-level information-theoretic properties but loses end-to-end protection
  against relay compromise.
- **Immediate operability:** Correct advantage.
- **No large-scale network:** “No large-scale untrusted-relay quantum internet” is likely correct but requires definitions
  and exact cutoff.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Essential honesty about deployed QKD.

- **Twin-field “production quality”:** Long-distance TF-QKD record experiments may not be production-engineering

- **Satellite operation:** Micius-style trusted demonstrations/services differ from routine always-available intercontinental
  key service.
- **NV “repeaters”:** Two-/three-node entanglement networks are not necessarily functioning repeater nodes; avoid
  relabeling components.
- **Second-scale memory:** Coherence alone does not show efficient entanglement storage/retrieval.
- **GHZ distribution:** Platform/distance/rate must be stated.
- **“Nowhere in world”:** Absence claim needs systematic current audit.

#### §33.6 — beyond-QKD opening

- **“Headline”:** Fair.
- **Pilot claim:** “Several” needs named demonstrations and a distinction among laboratory proof, field pilot and
  operational service.
- **Scope:** Applications require substantially more capable networks than prepare-and-measure QKD, so their readiness
  cannot be inferred from QKD deployment.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Promising transition.

#### §33.6 — distributed quantum sensing: theory

- **Global parameter:** Entangled networks can improve estimation of selected linear/global functions under synchronized
  phase references and a specified total resource. They do not generically reveal local fields better.
- **Heisenberg limit:** Loss/decoherence/distribution cost often destroys \(1/N\) scaling; count entanglement-generation
  photons/time/memories and successful postselection.
- **GHZ versus NOON:** Suitable for discrete sensors versus optical modes, respectively; not interchangeable without
  encoding context.
- **Local information:** Classical communication/correlations can estimate averages too; advantage needs optimal
  separable benchmark.
- **Cross-reference:** Verify §31.1 and carry its local-estimation/dynamic-range caveats.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Networked sensing is a natural payoff.

#### §33.6 — distributed-sensing demonstrations/forecasts

- **Highly current claims:** Identify exact 3–4-node experiments, medium, baseline, measured advantage, distance and year.
- **“Connected by short fiber”:** Some networked-sensor demonstrations may emulate channels or use shared optical fields
  rather than distributed stored GHZ states.
- **Field programs:** Name funder/project and milestone; “several ongoing” is vague.
- **Telescope proposal:** Quantum-assisted very-long-baseline interferometry is a proposal family requiring high-rate
  entanglement, quantum memories/transduction and loss tolerance—not simply a Heisenberg-limited EHT successor.
- **EHT wording:** VLBI already relies on classical correlations/atomic clocks; explain what quantum network changes.
- **Clock/dark matter:** Promising research directions, not demonstrated network applications.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Telescope-scale entanglement is spectacular.

#### §33.6 — blind quantum computing theorem/setup

- **Attribution:** Verify Broadbent–Fitzsimons–Kashefi 2009 paper/protocol and distinguish universal blind quantum
  computation (UBQC) from later verifiable/measurement-only variants.
- **Client capability:** Typically prepares randomly rotated single-qubit states from a finite set and sends them; it
  also performs classical adaptive instructions/one-time-pad updates.
- **“Nothing”:** Information-theoretic blindness has allowed leakage such as upper bounds on computation size/structure,
  depending padding; specify leakage and malicious-server model.
- **Output:** For classical output the client decrypts measurement results; quantum-output variants require additional
  capabilities/protocols.
- **Verification:** Blindness does not guarantee the server computed correctly; traps/verifiable BQC are separate.
- **MBQC link:** Correct and worth a concrete angle-masking equation.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Excellent security application.

#### §33.6 — blind-computing network analogy/composition

- **Quantum cloud:** Requires a quantum channel capable of client-to-server state transmission, authentication and loss
  handling—not a mature generic quantum network.
- **Homomorphic analogy:** Blind delegated computation resembles secure delegation and can be compared with homomorphic
  encryption, but functionality/security/interaction differ. Avoid “the quantum analog” as identity.
- **QKD composition:** QKD can provide keys/authenticated confidentiality for classical channels, but universal
  composability must be proven; “composes cleanly” is a theorem-level claim.
- **Redundancy:** UBQC’s blindness does not require QKD if classical authentication/encryption is otherwise provided.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Strong software-security bridge.

#### §33.6 — distributed-computing capacity premise

- **Hilbert dimension:** Tensor-product dimension multiplies, but networked modules do not automatically behave like a
  monolithic processor; nonlocal gate rate/fidelity, synchronization, memory and compiler partitioning define usable
  capacity.
- **Classical analogy:** Network cut/bisection bandwidth and communication complexity are central.
- **Application locality:** Algorithms with few cross-partition gates benefit most; arbitrary circuits can be dominated
  by ebits/latency.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Clear systems motivation.

#### §33.6 — remote-CNOT resource claim

- **Likely resource-count error:** A deterministic nonlocal CNOT with one shared ebit commonly uses local CNOTs,
  measurements at both nodes, and two classical bits total (one each direction), plus Pauli corrections. The text says
  “two single-qubit measurements, two classical bits, and one local correction at each node,” which may imply two bits
  total but needs an explicit circuit.
- **Gate teleportation terminology:** Standard gate teleportation via Choi/resource states can consume different
  entanglement. Remote CNOT is often called teleported CNOT; cite exact protocol.
- **One ebit:** Correct for a standard remote CNOT under ideal local operations.
- **Bandwidth condition:** Average ebit rate must cover nonlocal gate demand plus purification/error correction losses,
  bursts and latency; “exceed rate” alone is insufficient.
- **Logical operation:** Fault-tolerant remote logical gates require logical Bell pairs/error detection and far more
  physical resources.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** One ebit per remote gate makes network bandwidth concrete.

#### §33.6 — modular hardware/current demonstrations

- **Architecture claims:** Verify trapped-ion photonic interconnects, superconducting microwave-to-optical/direct
  interconnect proposals, and distinguish intra-cryostat modular couplers from a quantum network.
- **Record claim:** “First proof-of-principle two-module logical-qubit demonstrations appeared 2024–2025” is recent and
  potentially wrong. Name platform, paper, encoded logical qubit, deterministic/heralded gate, distance and fidelity.
- **“Logical-qubit”:** Experiments linking physical modules or teleporting gates are not necessarily logical/encoded.
- **Monolithic contrast:** Modular architectures may use chiplets/coherent microwave links without photonics.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Very current and compelling if sourced.

#### §33.6 — anonymous broadcasting/voting/Byzantine agreement

- **Protocol specificity:** GHZ states enable some anonymous transmission/veto/voting protocols under honest-majority,
  authenticated-channel, collision, abort and collusion assumptions; not a generic capability.
- **Voting privacy:** “Each announces a vote without revealing which vote came from whom” is internally odd—each party’s
  action can reveal participation/timing; protocols aim at ballot privacy/anonymity with defined tally leakage.
- **Byzantine claim:** “Stronger security than classical achievables” depends on synchrony, authentication, adversary
  fraction and setup. Quantum resources can change detectable broadcast/agreement bounds, but name theorem.
- **Lab demonstrations:** Each architecture/network size/security property requires citations; a physical GHZ demo is
  not automatically a full anonymous protocol.
- **Deployment:** Appropriately negative.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Multiparty protocols broaden the stakes.

#### §33.6 — clock synchronization

- **Advantage conditions:** Entanglement-assisted clock synchronization has reference-frame, transport-delay,
  decoherence and resource-counting subtleties; it does not generically surpass SQL in real networks.
- **Security:** Adversarial delay/asymmetry is a classical network/time-transfer problem entanglement does not
  automatically solve.
- **Evidence:** Distinguish theoretical proposals from experiments.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Natural but compressed.

#### §33.6 — quantum secret sharing

- **Shamir analogy:** Quantum secret sharing distributes a classical or quantum secret so authorized subsets can
  reconstruct; no-cloning imposes intersecting access structures for quantum secrets. It is not simply “Shamir with
  quantum states.”
- **Security:** Information-theoretic secrecy holds in ideal/proven models; authentication, cheater detection and noisy
  reconstruction matter.
- **Resource:** GHZ/CSS/stabilizer codes connect secret sharing to QEC; worth stating.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Useful bridge to familiar cryptography.

#### §33.6 — coin flipping/bit commitment

- **No-go precision:** Unconditionally secure quantum bit commitment is impossible in standard nonrelativistic models
  (Mayers/Lo–Chau), but relativistic, bounded/noisy-storage, computational and cheat-sensitive variants alter results.
- **Coin flipping:** Strong/weak quantum coin-flipping have nonzero optimal biases and distinct impossibility/achievability
  results; do not lump with bit commitment.
- **“Subset of no-go”:** Awkward wording. Explicitly list assumptions relaxed by each variant.
- **Application status:** Mostly theory/small demonstrations; correct.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Intriguing catalog ending.

#### §33.6 — beyond-key-distribution conclusion

- **“Catalog grows”:** Fine.
- **Evidence tiers:** Label theorem, lab demonstration, field pilot, operational service for every application; the
  paragraph’s main weakness is blending these.
- **Network capability:** Many proposals need universal nodes/memories far beyond long-distance QKD hardware.
- **Balanced conclusion:** Research demonstrations still justify investigating a more general network, but do not yet
  prove economic demand.
- **Entertainment: 4/5.** Sober last sentence.

#### Chapter 33 sanity check 1 — teleportation bookkeeping

- **Conceptual confusion:** The four Bell-expansion *terms* do not “supply the classical bits” or ebit. The ebit is the
  initial Bell pair; Alice’s Bell measurement yields one of four outcomes encoded by two cbits; Bob’s correction uses
  that message.
- **Correction table:** Ask readers to map each Bell outcome to \(I,Z,X,XZ\) under explicit Bell conventions.
- **Resource timing:** The ebit had to be distributed earlier; its creation cost is outside the primitive inequality.
- **Outcome privacy:** Adding proof that each outcome is uniformly random independent of \(|\psi\rangle\) would deepen the
  check.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Good identity check after wording repair.

#### Chapter 33 sanity check 2 — PLOB/twin-field arithmetic

- **100 km:** \(\eta=10^{-0.02(100)}=10^{-2}\). PLOB is
  \(-\log_2(0.99)\approx0.01450\) bits/use—not merely \(\eta=0.01\); the small-\(\eta\) factor \(1/\ln2\) matters.
- **500 km:** Fiber \(\eta=10^{-10}\). Comparing \(\sqrt\eta=10^{-5}\) to \(\eta=10^{-10}\) gives a five-order scaling
  improvement before constants/security overhead.
- **Incorrect direct comparison:** TF-QKD’s actual secret-key rate is not exactly \(\sqrt\eta\), while PLOB is
  \(\approx1.44\eta\); state this is an asymptotic scaling exercise.
- **Channel-use accounting:** Each TF trial sends pulses from two arms; network PLOB bounds and definitions matter.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Excellent distance intuition.

#### Chapter 33 sanity check 3 — repeater scaling

- **Memoryless arithmetic:** \(p^{n}=0.01^{10}=10^{-20}\), so expected simultaneous attempts \(10^{20}\), assuming
  independent synchronized attempts.
- **Underdetermined memory-assisted answer:** Merely knowing memory coherence exceeds round-trip time does not determine
  expected trials/rate. Link attempts may be parallel; swap probabilities, nesting, memory count, multiplexing,
  purification, attempt duration and scheduling are missing.
- **False request:** “Compare the two scalings explicitly” cannot yield a numeric memory-assisted result from the given
  data. Provide an ideal model (deterministic swaps, parallel links, unlimited memories) or ask qualitatively.
- **Coherence:** Must survive random maximum waiting time and swap/classical stages, not one round trip only.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** The \(10^{20}\) shock is powerful; incomplete second half.

#### Chapter 33 sanity check 4 — dense-coding information location

- **Correct insight:** Every Bell state has maximally mixed single-qubit marginals \(I/2\), so neither subsystem alone
  carries the two-bit message; it is encoded in joint correlations/global Bell state.
- **Nuance:** Alice’s encoding choice changes the joint state while each local reduced state remains fixed.
- **Capacity:** Bob needs both qubits/a joint Bell measurement and pre-shared entanglement.
- **Exercise quality:** Excellent and fully supported by the chapter.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Deep conceptual payoff from a small calculation.

#### Chapter 33 sanity check 5 — satellite-versus-fiber

- **dB arithmetic:** \(\eta_{\rm sat}=10^{-2}\) is 20 dB loss; \(\eta_{\rm fiber}=10^{-10}\) is 100 dB loss, so ideal
  transmittance advantage is 80 dB or \(10^8\).
- **Given inconsistency:** Earlier satellite paragraph says 10–30 dB, so fixing \(\eta\sim10^{-2}\) selects 20 dB; label

- **Loaded conclusion:** One link-budget number alone does not justify hundred-million-dollar missions. Coverage,

- **False comparison:** “Still-larger ground repeater networks” are not deployable; relevant alternatives include trusted

- **Mission cost:** “Hundred-million-dollar-class” needs sourced costs and should not be embedded as an answer the reader
  must defend.
- **Entertainment: 5/5.** Great scale comparison, overly rhetorical economics.
