Add test cases/traceability, baseline metrics, false-positive/negative tolerance, reviewer calibration/inter-rater agreement, conflicts, issue closure evidence, change impact, and quality tradeoff authority. Verdict: **one of the framework’s strongest plans, needing research ethics and method-specific sampling/stopping detail**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 391–395 — WP-03.09 compliance traceability plan

- Mapping source/jurisdiction/role/implementation/verifier/evidence/retention/review/exceptions is strong, and separating legal minimum from voluntary target is essential. “Responsible economic/operator role” appears imported from product regulation and may not fit publishing or all jurisdictions; define typed roles. The plan needs obligation ID/quoted requirement, authoritative version/hash, applicability rationale, affected product/market/format, control owner, test method/result, effective/expiry dates, legal interpretation/counsel, change alert, remediation and residual risk. Do not store privileged legal advice or personal data in broadly accessible matrices. Exceptions/exemptions require authority and cannot be self-declared; accessibility “exceptions” especially need narrow legal analysis and equivalent-access alternatives. Best practice may become contractual or advertised commitment, so track claim effects. Verdict: **strong compliance mapping skeleton with undefined regulatory terminology and exception authority**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 396–399 — WP-03.10 developmental-editing plan

- Planning developmental review at architecture, prototype, representative chapter, mid-manuscript, complete manuscript and pre-freeze stages can prevent expensive late restructuring. Six mandatory-looking passes may be disproportionate, duplicate Phase 6/7/8/9 reviews, or create churn if one editor lacks continuity; the phrase “as proportionate” needs a tailoring rubric. `{E}` as accountable default may be unavailable before acquisition or conflicted if the editor also approves. Define purpose, artifact maturity, reviewer competence/independence, questions/rubric, turnaround, author response, issue severity, acceptance/closure, continuity, version, budget and retest for each pass. “First representative chapter” should be risk-selected, not merely chronological. Accessibility/pedagogy/technical review overlap but are not substitutes for developmental editing. Verdict: **valuable staged editing strategy likely to duplicate later gates without pass-specific scopes and proportional tailoring**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 400–404 — WP-03.11 communication/adoption/marketing baseline

- Coordinating promotional claims with evidence, confidentiality, embargoes, rights and accessibility is excellent. The workstream repeats Phase 1.12 and needs a delta: approved positioning, claim registry, assets, schedule, owners/budget, channels and metrics after authorization. Endorsements/reviews require truthful quotation, permission, material-connection/compensation disclosure, no coercion, embargo and correction/withdrawal procedures. ARCs needs expansion and privacy/version/accessibility controls. Instructor/library/society outreach should follow consent/community norms and avoid spam; rights marketing may expose unpublished material. Add localization, metadata/SEO limits, accessible campaigns/events, crisis/correction communication, moderation, data protection for mailing/analytics, sustainability and anti-hype review. Route applicability should exclude confidential/internal projects. Verdict: **responsible claims-aware marketing baseline with substantial duplication and missing endorsement/data ethics**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.3/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 405–414 — Gate 3 project-baseline approval

- This is an appropriately serious readiness gate and uniquely requires testable quality/compliance criteria, bound independent checks, resourcing and live risk ownership. Evidence should include signed/versioned baselines, requirement catalogue/schema, schedule/capacity/cash flow, contracts/obligations, participant/research-ethics plan, accessibility baseline, security/privacy controls, backup restore result, representative—not minimal—build, dependency/license inventory, maintenance funding and unresolved conditions. “Live registers” does not prove completeness/currentness and the framework still has not identified their system of record. “Work is resourced” needs committed people/budget/time, not estimates; “toolchain works” needs representative acceptance tests; “gaps have remedies” needs owners/deadlines and acceptable residual risk. Route confirmation may still have contract contingencies. Failure can require reopening Gates 1/2, not just Phase 3 replanning, and must define what work may continue. Verdict: **strong readiness checkpoint that cannot currently be evidenced because its atomic catalogue/register infrastructure remains unspecified**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 415–416 — Phase 4 research/compliance groundwork scope

- This phase correctly front-loads evidence, ethics, data, permissions and compliance before architecture/drafting. “Groundwork” understates controls that must continue through publication, and the title omits source surveillance, research integrity, security/privacy and accessibility packages included later. Research and compliance work can run in parallel but have stop dependencies (ethics/permissions before collection/use) that need a map. Verdict: **well-positioned evidence phase whose “groundwork” label risks implying later completion rather than continuous control**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 417–422 — WP-04.01 research strategy and method

- Requiring questions, reproducible search strategy, inclusion/exclusion, evidence standards, currency, stopping and surveillance is excellent. The method list contains overlapping review traditions and specialized legal/technical searches; selecting one or more needs competence, protocol, databases, languages, dates, search strings, deduplication, screening, extraction, appraisal and synthesis plans. “Narrative” is not an excuse for opaque selection. Systematic review should be required by claim/purpose and relevant disciplinary standards, as stated, but the trigger needs criteria and registration/reporting guidance. Historical/archival work needs provenance/source criticism; patent/standards searches have legal scope and coverage limits. Completion is never “all evidence found”; define saturation/last search and residual uncertainty. Add living-review triggers, grey literature, citation chaining, automation/AI validation, dual screening where warranted, protocol deviations and public protocol where safe. Verdict: **excellent method-aware research charter needing reproducible protocol fields and method-specific standards**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 423–427 — WP-04.02 source discovery and evaluation

- The source universe and appraisal factors are unusually broad, including negative results, preprints, corrections, funding and conflicts. Source type does not determine authority: official docs can market, peer review can fail, preprints can be rigorous, standards/patents encode institutional incentives, and expert testimony needs credentials/conflicts/recording. Add study design-specific bias tools, sample/applicability, statistical power/multiplicity, data/code availability, citation context, publication bias, language/geographic bias, predatory venues, image/data integrity, provenance/authenticity and corroboration. Retraction/correction checks need dates and automated alerts. Patents establish claims/priority documents, not efficacy or freedom to operate. “Replicability” may be unknown; distinguish reproducibility, replication and robustness. Evaluation should be recorded per source with calibrated ratings and independent checks for pivotal evidence. Verdict: **strong appraisal checklist requiring source-type-specific rubrics and protection against authority-by-category**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 428–433 — WP-04.03 evidence and claim management

- This is a core strength: page-level quotations, contradictory evidence, uncertainty, claim type, assumptions and validity conditions can prevent unsupported prose. Yet “each material claim” needs a materiality/volatility/risk rule; full claim atomization can become unmanageable. The type taxonomy overlaps: definitions can be facts/conventions, derived results depend on assumptions, empirical findings may be facts, recommendations mix evidence and values. Permit multiple facets and record normative/value premises. “Hidden assumptions” cannot be known by definition; record identified implicit assumptions and search for unknowns. Add claim ID/text/version/location, source-specific support/contradiction relation, directness, evidence grade/method, reviewer/date, citation/page/quote rights, as-of/expiry, downstream dependencies, verification result and change propagation. Quotations/pages differ by edition and require copyright limits. A reference manager alone is not a claim graph. Verdict: **excellent claim-discipline design needing scalable materiality rules and a normalized evidence-relation schema**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 434–439 — WP-04.04 research synthesis

- Preserving disagreement, negative results, boundaries and limitations is exemplary. “Evidence-weighted” requires a declared synthesis method; otherwise author judgment can manufacture either consensus or false balance. Distinguish quantitative meta-analysis, qualitative/thematic synthesis, historical narrative, standards comparison and expert elicitation, with heterogeneity, bias, certainty and applicability methods. Consensus should not be head-counting, and minority views should be weighted by evidence rather than symmetry. Add stakeholder/value conflicts, temporal/geographic variation, causal versus correlational claims, sensitivity analyses, excluded evidence and author positionality/conflicts. Linking conclusions to architecture/examples/exclusions is excellent but needs traceable IDs and change propagation when evidence updates. Independent review should focus on high-impact synthesis judgments. Verdict: **responsible synthesis principles without the method needed to make “evidence-weighted” reproducible**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 440–444 — WP-04.05 original research and empirical work

- The design checklist is strong and includes preregistration, power, controls, calibration, deviations and negative results. A book is often a poor first/only venue for original research because review, update and data constraints differ; require a route decision on prior peer-reviewed publication, registered report, protocol or transparent supplementary report. Ethics review should precede *all* human/animal or sensitive-data work where required by institution/jurisdiction, not merely work someone labels “regulated”; exempt determinations should come from authorized bodies. Add consent, recruitment/compensation, privacy/security, data-monitoring, adverse events, stopping rules, registration ID, analysis code/environment, estimands, missing data, multiplicity, effect sizes/uncertainty, robustness, authorship/COI/funding, reporting checklists, material transfer/export and replication. Safety/provenance records may require restricted access. Verdict: **strong empirical checklist missing publication-route, participant-protection and statistical reproducibility detail**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 445–450 — WP-04.06 data and artifact management

- The lifecycle coverage and proportionate FAIR commitment are excellent, as are availability statements, restrictions, PIDs and maintenance responsibility. FAIR accessibility does not mean open access; explicitly state authentication/controlled access can be FAIR. Anonymization is often reversible or impossible for rich datasets, so require minimization, lawful basis/consent, threat modeling, pseudonymization, de-identification assessment, data-use agreements and breach response. Add data management plan/version/schema/validation, integrity/fixity, lineage, quality, sensitive classification, encryption/key management, deletion, participant withdrawal limits, jurisdiction/data residency, repository certification, costs/succession and disaster-recovery tests. Code/artifacts need environment/dependency/container/SBOM, tests, licenses, citation (`CITATION.cff`), releases/checksums and executable preservation. Indigenous/community data may require CARE or local sovereignty principles beyond FAIR. Verdict: **excellent FAIR-aware lifecycle skeleton needing privacy realism, code reproducibility and community data governance**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 451–455 — WP-04.07 research integrity and ethics

- Integrity principles are mandatory for every project, so classifying the whole package `[RISK]` could make honesty, citation integrity and authorship conditional; split `[CORE]` integrity from type/risk-dependent research ethics. `[APPROVE]` is also wrong for ongoing conduct: plan, implement, verify, disclose and maintain, with authorized ethics approvals only where applicable. Add fabrication/falsification, selective reporting, image/data manipulation, paper mills/citation coercion, duplicate publication, peer-review confidentiality, whistleblowing/nonretaliation, misconduct allegation/appeal, corrections/retractions and institutional processes. Text-reuse/plagiarism tools have false positives and privacy/license implications; human contextual review is required. Authorship/credit needs discipline criteria and change logs. Community/cultural protections require engagement, sovereignty, benefit sharing and local protocols, not only approval. Conflicts/funding need ongoing updates and management, not disclosure alone. Verdict: **essential ethics content misclassified as conditional and reduced to an approval-stage package**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 456–461 — WP-04.08 rights and permissions groundwork

- The asset inventory and granular permission fields are excellent, especially accessibility adaptation rights, territories, formats and expiry. `[SELECT:ONE]` is too rigid: an author-owned asset can also be openly licensed; a composite figure can contain public-domain, licensed and permissioned elements; publisher ownership may coexist with author reuse rights. Use per-component rights bundles and provenance. “Public domain” and statutory exceptions are jurisdiction/use specific; require qualified case analysis, documented four-factor/fair-dealing or quotation-right reasoning, and contingency—not a universal label. “Publisher-owned” is not itself permission. Track creator/source, original/license version/link, modifications, moral/personality/privacy/trademark rights, model/property releases, sublicensing, AI provenance, font embedding, code/data license compatibility, attribution placement, fee/payment, revocation and evidence hash. Standards/maps/media often have special restrictions. Verdict: **strong rights ledger undermined by mutually exclusive asset classification and jurisdiction-sensitive shorthand**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 462–468 — WP-04.09 safety/security/privacy/defamation/dual-use controls

- The perimeter is exceptionally broad and appropriately includes capability escalation, secret removal, redaction, right of reply, distributional effects and foreseeable misuse. One `[RISK] {J}` package cannot supply competence across physical safety, biosafety, medicine, cybersecurity, privacy, defamation and societal impact; route each domain to qualified reviewers/legal counsel and relevant authorities. Define screening thresholds, threat/risk models, severity, protected evidence, need-to-know access, escalation, emergency stop, incident/vulnerability coordination, embargo, appeal and residual-risk authority. Secure-code review needs dependency/SBOM, static/dynamic/manual testing and safe example isolation; never publish live credentials/exploitable targets. Anonymization is not guaranteed. Defamation review must distinguish documented allegation/opinion/public interest/jurisdiction and protect legitimate criticism; right of reply needs deadlines and non-veto status. Dual-use redaction must preserve scientific usefulness/reproducibility proportionately. Societal/sustainability assessment needs stakeholder input and method. Verdict: **excellent hazard map requiring specialist subcontrols and protected decision processes to become safe**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 469–476 — WP-04.10 accessibility applicability and baseline

- This is unusually sophisticated in separating law/contract from best practice and refusing automatic legal-presumption claims from WCAG/EPUB alone. Accessibility planning should not be only `[JUR]`: inclusive source and usable outputs are a CORE quality aim even absent law; legal applicability is the conditional layer. “Economic operator,” fundamental alteration and disproportionate burden are jurisdiction-specific concepts and must not be generalized or self-declared. Exemptions need qualified authority, evidence, approval, expiry/reassessment and equivalent-access mitigation. Dated frameworks must include exact version/conformance level, product/format, test method, AT/browser/device matrix and responsible party. Engage disabled readers and accessibility specialists with compensation/privacy; automated testing alone is insufficient. Include print/large print, braille/structured source, cognitive/plain-language, captions/transcripts/audio description, color/tactile considerations, equations/code/tables/figures, DRM and accessible customer support. Verdict: **excellent legal caution with accessibility itself incorrectly framed as merely jurisdiction-conditional**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.7/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 477–480 — WP-04.11 AI-use applicability and governance

- Determining whether AI rules apply should be CORE because even a prohibition/nonuse assertion needs scope and tools may embed AI invisibly; actual use is risk-conditional. The one-line list is far too compressed for a canonical framework. Define AI/system/use categories, model/provider/version/date, input/output types, permitted data, purpose, user, human review, accuracy/verification, provenance, prompt/output retention, confidentiality/data residency/training/opt-out, security, copyright/license, bias/accessibility, disclosure/attribution, consent, image/voice/translation impersonation, vendor terms, cost/environmental impact and incident handling. Publisher/institution/funder/law rules can conflict; set precedence and escalation. “Human accountability” is excellent but requires named decision authority and cannot imply a human merely rubber-stamps output. Records may expose confidential prompts/personal data and need minimization/access/retention. Governance must adapt when policies/models change. Verdict: **correct governance categories compressed far below the framework’s otherwise granular standard**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.3/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 481–487 — WP-04.12 copyright/licensing/deposit/localization plan

- Separating copyright registration from legal deposit is an excellent and often-missed distinction, and license compatibility across book/code/data/media is essential. Copyright protection/registration/remedies are jurisdiction-specific; avoid implying one universal registration strategy and require counsel where material. Compatibility needs a dependency/rights matrix covering copyleft, attribution, database rights, moral rights, patents, fonts, model releases, trademarks, third-party publisher terms, OA license, source versus output and collective work. Legal deposit duties vary by publisher of record, format, country, timing, accessibility and update/edition. Localization is not just legal: plan translator qualifications/credit/compensation, source freeze/version alignment, translation memory/data privacy, right-to-left/layout expansion, cultural adaptation, accessibility, localized examples/links/law, code/UI strings, QA/back-translation where appropriate and update propagation. “Source-language control” needs an authoritative-language and discrepancy process. Verdict: **strong legal/localization bridge needing a rights matrix and full translation quality lifecycle**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 488–491 — WP-04.13 ongoing surveillance

- Continuous alerts for papers, corrections, standards, software, data, policy and security are essential for a current technical book. `{A}` alone is inappropriate: legal, security, publisher, software, data and research alerts need distributed qualified owners and a maintainer after handoff. Define sources/subscriptions, query/version, cadence, cutoff, deduplication, triage severity/SLA, evidence update, affected-claim tracing, freeze exceptions, notification, correction/release and closure. Alerts are not proof of monitoring; retain logs and test that feeds work. Add law/regulation, vulnerabilities/CVEs, dependency EOL, license/terms, retractions of cited sources, broken links and competitor/classical-baseline changes where relevant. Prevent alert fatigue and distinguish prepublication surveillance from postpublication maintenance funding. Verdict: **vital living-book control stated only as a source list, without an operational monitoring/response loop**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 492–501 — Gate 4 evidence/compliance readiness

- The evidence bundle appropriately brings research, ethics, artifacts, permissions, safety/privacy, accessibility/AI and normative references together before architecture. There is a serious sequencing defect: WP-04.05 is tagged `[IMPLEMENT]` and includes original empirical work, but Gate 4 only now requires regulated work to be authorized *before execution*. Ethics/safety/privacy authorization must be an entry condition or internal hold point before any participant/data/hazard activity, not an end-of-phase criterion. “Regulated work” is too narrow; institutional ethics, consent, community governance and high-risk unregulated work may also require approval. “Central claims have a plausible evidence path” is weak and undefined; record evidence sufficiency/gaps and prohibited claims. “Risks are identified and controlled” overclaims unknown risks and incomplete early controls. Add rights/license compatibility, legal advice/status, AI-use records, surveillance operation, source-search reproducibility, data security, research protocol/registration, accessibility baseline, specialist sign-offs and unresolved conditions. Failure may require stopping/destructively quarantining unauthorized work, reporting incidents and reopening prior gates—not only revising plans. Verdict: **important readiness gate placed too late to prevent unauthorized original research and governed by vague plausibility/control criteria**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 502–503 — Phase 5 architecture/pedagogy scope

- This phase correctly waits for evidence groundwork before committing structure and includes accessible source plus developmental validation rather than treating them as production afterthoughts. Its title is long but still omits navigation, dependency design and localization readiness. Architecture must remain revisable when prototype/review evidence changes; define baseline rather than freeze. Verdict: **well-sequenced design phase with a mutable-architecture contract left implicit**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 504–508 — WP-05.01 central narrative and knowledge model

- The inventory of concepts through critiques/limitations is strong, but a “principal thesis,” “central narrative,” and final synthesis do not fit every handbook, reference, edited volume or multi-perspective work. Permit organizing questions, task taxonomy, knowledge graph or modular reference architecture. “Foundational question” can manufacture unity and teleology; preserve plural/contested models and uncertainty. The package needs concept IDs, definitions/sources, relations/dependencies, validity domains, terminology links, claim/evidence links, audience level, examples/counterexamples and change ownership. Distinguish conceptual model from rhetorical narrative so elegant storytelling cannot override evidence. Test the model with subject experts and target readers, including what is excluded or nonhierarchical. Verdict: **strong coherence design that assumes a single thesis/narrative beyond the framework’s declared book types**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 509–513 — WP-05.02 dependency and abstraction design

- Explicitly finding prerequisites, forward/circular dependencies, missing bridges and optional/reference branches is excellent. The proposed ladder is useful but not universal: intuition before definition can seed misconceptions, “informal model” after precise definition is oddly ordered, implementation may motivate theory earlier, and critique/limits should accompany rather than always end a topic. Label it a pattern library and test alternatives. Define dependency types (hard/soft, conceptual/procedural, notation/tool), concept versions, assumed prior knowledge, branch rejoin points and diagnostics/remediation. A graph should detect cycles/orphans and drive reading paths/cross-links; intentional spirals need a progression contract rather than duplicate definitions. Accessibility/cognitive load and assessment alignment belong in dependency decisions. Verdict: **excellent prerequisite discipline with an overly linear default ladder and no executable dependency graph**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 514–520 — WP-05.03 book/chapter/sequence/scope architecture

- The coverage is excellent and explicitly keeps chapter elements optional, avoiding a rigid template. The many sequencing principles can conflict—concrete before abstract versus prerequisite formalism, spiral reinforcement versus redundancy, theory–practice alternation versus coherent derivation—so require selected principles, rationale and reader-test evidence. Chapter patterns need purpose-specific variants, not arbitrary menu picks. Content tiers are valuable but need decision criteria, owner, page/word/production budget, dependency effects and status; “online-only” introduces access, preservation, version and parity risks, while deferred content needs a future owner/date or true exclusion. References/index/glossary planning this early is strong. Add learning/dependency/claim coverage matrices, visual/code/data/artifact budgets, cross-format constraints, change thresholds and architecture traceability to success outcomes. Verdict: **excellent flexible architecture menu without tradeoff rules or budgeted traceability**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 521–530 — WP-05.04 pedagogy and reader pathways

- This is exceptionally comprehensive: outcomes, diagnostics, cognitive load, misconceptions, retrieval/interleaving, assessment varieties and paths are all valuable. `[TYPE]` is questionable because every book intended to teach or support professional tasks needs reader-learning/information-use design; only formal curriculum/assessment elements are type-conditional. Section-level measurable outcomes may create bureaucracy and atomized reading; choose outcome granularity based on use. Learning-science techniques should be evidence- and audience-appropriate, not mechanically mandated; repetition can aid learning while harming reference usability. Reader labels risk stereotypes and overlapping identities; define goal/prerequisite/time-based paths validated with users. Assessments need answer/solution policy, rubrics, difficulty, feedback, accessibility, academic-integrity/AI implications, safety, tooling/data and instructor support. Include motivation, metacognition, transfer, worked-example fading, prior-knowledge activation and affect/belonging carefully. Verdict: **one of the framework’s best packages, needing proportional granularity and nonstereotyped, evidence-tested pathways**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.8/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 531–534 — WP-05.05 navigation design

- The navigation elements are appropriate across linear and selective reading, but “page-navigation source” is undefined—perhaps running heads/page references or canonical anchors. Navigation must be format-specific: print folios/running heads/index, EPUB landmarks/TOC, PDF bookmarks/tags, web breadcrumbs/search/URLs, audio navigation and interactive state. Cross-references require stable IDs, automated validation, semantic link text, bidirectional context and graceful print/digital rendering. Reading paths need prerequisite/dependency validation and progress/resume cues; signposts/recaps can become repetitive. Meaningful links need accessibility, external-link policy, archives, version/date and link-rot monitoring. Index strategy duplicates 5.3 and later production; distinguish conceptual indexing plan from generated final locators. Verdict: **strong navigation checklist with an undefined term and no cross-format/link-maintenance model**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 535–543 — WP-05.06 terminology/notation/units/style system

- The scope is impressively complete across prose, math, code, visuals and citations. It needs one normative style/term registry with IDs, definition, scope, rationale, examples, exceptions, source, owner and lintability; lists alone will drift. Preferred/deprecated/culturally sensitive terms require affected-community/domain consultation and versioning, not unilateral labels. Acronym/symbol collision detection should be automated across chapters and formats. Units need SI policy plus field/legal exceptions, conversions, significant figures and dimensional checks. Mathematical conventions require basis/order, inner-product, indices, domains and equality/approximation. Code needs supported environments, licensing, testing, security and output determinism beyond style. Visual rules need color-independent encoding, alt/long description/tactile implications and grayscale/print tests. Citation policy should cover claim placement, primary/secondary hierarchy, software/data/standards, archival URLs and retractions. Define precedence among publisher, discipline, locale and project styles. Verdict: **excellent style-system perimeter needing a single governed, testable registry and precedence rules**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 544–547 — WP-05.07 accessible/localization-ready source

- Making accessible source CORE is excellent and partially corrects Phase 4’s jurisdiction-only framing. The list covers semantics, math/tables, descriptions, color, links, language, navigation, index, terminology, graphics and locale-sensitive data. `[PLAN]` is insufficient: source rules must be implemented continuously, linted, manually tested and regression-checked. “Accessible mathematics” needs MathML/structured alternatives, speech/braille testing, notation definitions and fallback; tables need headers/scope/captions and avoidance of layout tables. Alt text versus long description depends on informational purpose and surrounding text; decorative images need null alternatives. Controlled language can flatten authorial voice or introduce cultural bias; use clarity/translation guidance proportionately. Localization readiness also needs Unicode/fonts, bidi/vertical text, text expansion, plural/gender, sorting/index collation, examples/law/culture, screenshots/UI, captions/transcripts, code/string externalization, source-version alignment and translator notes. “Page navigation” varies by format. Verdict: **excellent source-first accessibility principle needing implementation states and concrete multimodal/localization mechanics**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 548–553 — WP-05.08 architecture-level developmental edit

- Reviewing promise, scope, dependencies, bridges, pacing, cognitive load, accessibility and production feasibility before full drafting is high leverage. “Resolve architecture-level issues” is absolute; some uncertainty can only be tested in Phase 6, so record disposition, residual risk, prototype question and conditional acceptance. `{E}` needs competence in the book type/audience and coordination with technical/accessibility specialists; one developmental editor cannot verify every listed domain. Define artifact/version, rubric, representative reader evidence, issue severity, author response, accepted/rejected rationale, escalation, retest and closure. Independence/conflicts matter if the editor helped design the architecture. Production feasibility should use actual vendor/tool constraints. Prevent endless restructuring with decision thresholds while preserving change control. Verdict: **high-value early edit with unrealistic total-resolution language and undefined multidisciplinary evidence**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 554–563 — Gate 5 architecture approval

- The evidence package is strong and appropriately includes dependency/path maps, controlled terminology, accessible-source specification, allocation and editor response. Calling architecture “final” before the full-stack prototype/reader validation is misleading; baseline it conditionally and expect Gate 6 evidence to reopen it. A coherent “thesis” is not applicable to every reference/edited book—use organizing purpose/model. “Readers have viable paths” cannot be proven before target-reader testing; at this gate it is a reviewed hypothesis. “Source can support outputs/accessibility” similarly requires the Phase 6 production prototype, so define provisional feasibility criteria. Add word/page/visual/artifact budget, claim/evidence coverage, prerequisite diagnostics, format-specific navigation, localization strategy, unresolved prototype questions, risk/change thresholds and representative-content selection. Failure correctly reaches evidence/product strategy but should reopen prior gates when scope/route changes. Verdict: **excellent architecture baseline gate that prematurely labels unprototyped reader and output feasibility as approved fact**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 564–565 — Phase 6 prototype/validation scope

- A full-stack prototype before full drafting is one of the framework’s best sequencing choices, since it can falsify architecture, production and reader assumptions cheaply. “Full-stack” needs a defined boundary spanning source through each intended output, distribution/accessibility and maintenance—not merely a sample build. Verdict: **high-leverage validation phase requiring an explicit stack/coverage definition**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 566–569 — WP-06.01 risk-based prototype selection

- Risk-based selection is far superior to simply choosing Chapter 1, and the candidate content dimensions are useful. “Smallest set” can under-test interacting risks; use set-cover logic plus critical end-to-end combinations and document residual uncovered risks. `[SELECT:ONE_OR_MORE]` is mandatory but selection criteria, risk traceability and approval are absent. A single sample may not represent beginner/advanced, math/code/data, print/digital, accessibility/localization and supplementary workflows; permit multiple thin vertical slices. “A project is not required to produce nonexistent chapter types” is tautological and likely means inapplicable content types. Include volatile claims, third-party permissions, longest/most complex equations/tables, indexing, dynamic/interactive media, bidi/localization, offline/low-bandwidth and failure/recovery cases. Record why omitted risks are acceptable. Verdict: **excellent risk-first principle without a coverage model for interactions and residual gaps**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 570–573 — WP-06.02 full-stack prototype implementation

- The artifact list is broad, but a single bullet does not define “through” the intended stack. Require representative source, review workflow, automated/manual checks, deterministic build, all target formats, packaging/metadata, accessibility tree/tags, localization transform, archival deposit, distribution preview and maintenance update. Code/data need environment, tests, expected outputs, licenses, security and reproducibility; equations/figures/tables need cross-format semantics and alternatives; exercises need solutions/rubrics. Use actual fonts/styles/templates and realistic file sizes. Third-party permissions and citations should exercise production placement. Capture versions/configuration, logs, checksums, timing/cost and defects. A prototype must include failure modes, not only a happy path. Verdict: **correct full-stack ingredients stated too tersely to guarantee an end-to-end production slice**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 574–578 — WP-06.03 toolchain/production validation

- Build, generation, conversion, accessibility, archival export, repository and recovery testing form an excellent minimum, especially the often-omitted recovery test. “Accessibility scan” is insufficient; combine automated checks with keyboard/screen-reader/AT/manual semantic/visual testing in every intended format. Validate deterministic/reproducible builds on a clean independent environment, dependency/license/security/SBOM, broken links, fonts, color/grayscale, print proof, EPUB/PDF validators, metadata, index/cross-reference integrity, performance/file size and offline behavior. Recovery must restore source, secrets/config references and build capability from backup, with RTO/RPO evidence. Migration/change control should include rollback rehearsal and output diffs. Publisher/vendor proprietary conversion may break the local result; test handoff round-trip. Verdict: **strong validation backbone whose single “scan” and generic build leave major format/reproducibility checks implicit**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 579–582 — WP-06.04 expert/developmental prototype review

- Reviewing technical content and editorial, pedagogical, production, accessibility, localization and maintenance feasibility together is valuable, but `{R/E}` as an alternative accountable role conflicts with the multidisciplinary list. One editor cannot verify science or accessibility, and one technical reviewer cannot validate pedagogy/localization. Assign domain-specific reviewers with qualification, independence, conflicts and a coverage matrix. Define artifacts/version, rubric/criteria, sample limitations, severity, evidence, response/disposition, dissent, retest and closure. Expert review should reproduce key derivations/code/data rather than only read, where applicable. Developmental reviewers involved in design are not independent verification. Include target-market/legal/publisher production constraints through qualified inputs. Verdict: **excellent cross-domain review scope incorrectly assignable to one alternative R-or-E role**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 583–589 — WP-06.05 target-reader testing

- Think-aloud, comprehension, tasks, navigation, delayed recall, AT interaction, confusion/abandonment and predeclared thresholds constitute unusually mature reader testing. It requires an ethical research protocol: consent, privacy, recording/transcription, compensation, recruitment diversity/bias, accommodations, withdrawal, secure retention, vulnerable participants and ethics determination. “Target reader” is plural across pathways; sample rationale must cover goals/prerequisites/languages/disabilities/devices without tokenizing. Think-aloud can alter cognition; delayed recall needs interval/control and attrition planning. Define tasks, scoring/inter-rater reliability, baseline/comparator, quantitative uncertainty and qualitative analysis/saturation. Accessibility testing should include disabled users where safe/consensual, not only proxy AT checks. Abandonment may reflect context rather than content. Report negative/unintended paths and avoid overgeneralizing small samples. Verdict: **exceptionally strong testing concept needing full human-research and measurement-quality controls**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.8/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 590–594 — WP-06.06 prototype revision and retest

- Revising architecture, scope, explanation, accessibility, tools, schedule and budget from evidence is exactly the purpose of prototyping, and impact-based retesting is efficient. Add issue-to-change traceability, before/after artifact versions, decision rationale, rejected feedback, regression suite, new-risk assessment, reviewer/participant recontact rules and baseline/gate reopening thresholds. Retest only affected criteria can miss emergent interactions; require risk-based regression plus periodic/full critical-path rerun. Schedule/budget/product/route changes may reopen Gates 1–5 or contracts, not remain local. Prevent overfitting to a small participant sample and preserve successful controls. Define closure/acceptance and maximum iteration/stop/pivot criteria. Verdict: **sound evidence-to-revision loop needing broader regression and prior-gate impact rules**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 595–598 — WP-06.07 early-access decision

- The decision fields wisely cover audience, embargo, versioning, feedback, moderation, disclosure, revision and withdrawal. Add purpose/hypothesis, eligibility/consent, accessibility parity, pricing/refunds, licenses/terms, privacy/analytics, security, support SLAs, citation/permalink policy, archival snapshots, known defects, no-reliance warnings, rights/permissions, participant/community safety and conversion to final access. Early public content can establish priority, trigger defamation/copyright/export issues, leak confidential material, become permanently cached and create citation/version confusion; withdrawal is not erasure. Feedback moderation needs conduct, appeals and labor. Define success/stop criteria and distinguish ARC, beta, open peer review and paid early access. Verdict: **good early-access skeleton underestimating permanence, participant rights and commercial/support obligations**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 599–610 — Gate 6 prototype approval

- The evidence bundle and explicit non-author involvement are strong. Pass criteria remain subjective: “representative,” “proportionately,” “stable,” “feasible” and “acceptable” must resolve to the predeclared coverage/quality/risk thresholds. A small prototype can demonstrate plausibility, not general reader fit or whole-book maintainability. “At least one qualified non-author verifier *or approver*” is too weak: a non-author approver relying on author-only verification does not provide independent verification, and one person cannot cover technical, reader, accessibility and production domains. Require independent verification for critical applicable domains with conflicts/qualifications. Add complete risk-coverage map, clean reproducible build/results, accessibility/manual AT evidence, reader ethics, issue closure/residual risk, cost/time metrics, rights/license check, archive/recovery and prior-gate impact approvals. Toolchain stability needs versioned baseline and supply-chain plan. Failure should explicitly reopen affected gates/contracts. Verdict: **excellent prototype checkpoint weakened by vague pass language and a minimal independence rule that permits no independent verification**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.7/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 611–612 — Phase 7 manuscript/artifact loop scope

- Treating manuscript and artifacts as one development loop is excellent; it discourages code/data/figures from becoming late attachments. The phase needs an explicit per-chapter iteration/acceptance state model and integration cadence, since “loop” alone does not prevent batch drafting or artifact drift. Verdict: **correct integrated-development principle without executable loop control**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 613–617 — WP-07.01 chapter initiation

- A chapter brief with purpose, dependencies, sources, inventories and acceptance criteria is strong. The inventory set is extensive and may create ceremony before discovery; use risk/type-based templates and allow progressive elaboration. “Book’s thesis” again excludes modular/reference/edited architectures; use organizing purpose/model. Source packets can freeze evidence prematurely and must link live claim surveillance, versions and cutoff dates. Include audience/path, outcomes, scope exclusions, word/page/visual/code budget, prerequisite diagnostic/remediation, volatile claims, safety/ethics, localization, reviewer roles, schedule, interfaces with adjacent chapters and definition ownership. Acceptance criteria need measurable evidence and change control. Avoid duplicating registers—reference IDs. Verdict: **excellent chapter contract at risk of duplicative bureaucracy and thesis-centric assumptions**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 618–623 — WP-07.02 drafting and section-level control

- The content progression and explicit separation of fact/derivation/interpretation/hypothesis/recommendation/opinion are exemplary. Motivation/formalism/examples need not follow one repeated order; use chapter architecture. Author-tagged `[VERIFY]` appears to permit self-verification of supported claims, cognitive load and terminology; distinguish author checks from independent later acceptance. “Clear,” “logical,” and controlled cognitive load need rubrics/reader evidence. Add claim IDs/citation proximity, assumptions/validity, counterexamples, uncertainty, accessibility semantics, cross-format navigation, definition/notation first-use, link/reference checks, inclusive language and stale-content flags. Transitions can become formulaic. Section-level status should record drafted/reviewed/verified/approved with artifact hash and issues. Automated lint cannot judge conceptual truth. Verdict: **strong drafting discipline conflating author quality control with verification and leaving qualitative criteria unmeasured**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 624–628 — WP-07.03 mathematical/formal content

- Premises, scopes, intermediate reasoning, edge/limit cases, dimensional checks and validity conditions form an excellent rigor checklist. Not every proof should show every intermediate step; calibrate to audience and provide expandable supplements. Dimensional checks do not apply to dimensionless/pure abstract work and cannot prove correctness. Add quantifiers/domains, existence/uniqueness, notation conventions, equality/approximation/error bounds, units, numerical conditioning, branch/sign/order conventions, counterexamples and machine-verifiable identities where feasible. Proof/dependency links need stable theorem/equation IDs and cycle/orphan checks. Collision checking should span meanings/scopes and formats. Author implementation still needs independent mathematical verification and executable symbolic/numerical checks for high-risk results. Cite standard results and distinguish proof from sketch/intuition. Verdict: **excellent mathematical rigor perimeter needing audience calibration and formal/independent verification links**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 629–635 — WP-07.04 code and algorithms

- The package wisely includes assumptions, invariants, complexity, stability, portability, security, errors, outputs, failure modes and archival releases. “No unnecessary complexity” is subjective; prioritize concept, production realism and safe simplicity explicitly. Algorithms need correctness argument, termination, pseudocode/code correspondence, access/input model, resource units, approximation/probability, baselines and licensing/patent caveats. Code needs supported versions/platforms, dependencies/SBOM, license/attribution, secrets, safe defaults, error handling, logging, accessibility, data privacy and deprecation/EOL. Focused excerpts can drift from complete versions; generate/test excerpts or map line/version hashes. “Where useful” runnable versions is too weak for code-bearing claims—state exceptions. CI proportionate criteria, branch protection, release signing/checksums, vulnerability handling and maintenance ownership are missing. Verdict: **strong code-content specification needing executable-excerpt synchronization and supply-chain/license controls**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 636–641 — WP-07.05 code testing/computational reproducibility

- The test taxonomy and repeatability/reproducibility/replicability/generalizability distinction are excellent. Not every project needs every test type, so “as applicable” needs risk mapping and coverage evidence. Add static/type/lint, fuzz, mutation, concurrency, API/contract, accessibility and supply-chain/license tests selectively. Performance tests require benchmark environment, warm-up, variance and regression thresholds; security tests need safe scope and specialist review. Seeds do not guarantee determinism across libraries/hardware; record RNG algorithms, precision, concurrency and tolerance rationale. Locks/containers need archived dependencies/images and rebuilds on clean independent systems; hardware/cloud identifiers/calibration matter. Expected outputs may be statistical distributions. CI logs/artifacts/checksums, test coverage limitations, flaky-test policy, failure triage, platform matrix/EOL and reproduction time/cost are needed. `[VERIFY/IMPLEMENT]` mixes correction with independent result status. Verdict: **excellent reproducibility checklist needing risk-based coverage, independent clean builds and nondeterminism realism**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.7/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 642–647 — WP-07.06 experimental/data content

- The package comprehensively covers apparatus through deviations and data transformations through uncertainty/negative results. It duplicates Phase 4 original research/data planning and must link approved protocol/ethics rather than silently permit new experiments during drafting. Any deviation affecting participant safety/consent or validity needs authorized review before continuation where possible. Add timestamps/versioned protocols, operators, environment, instrument firmware/software, measurement traceability, blinding/randomization, sample-size rationale, exclusions, missing-data mechanism, preprocessing provenance, estimands, multiplicity, effect sizes/confidence, model diagnostics and analysis code. “Publish raw data” must be subordinate to consent, privacy, security, Indigenous/community governance, commercial/confidential and legal restrictions; FAIR controlled access/preservation may be correct. Anonymization is not a guarantee. Reproduction instructions need independent test and preserved apparatus limitations. Verdict: **strong empirical reporting package with a dangerous need to bind all work to prior ethics/protocol authorization**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 648–653 — WP-07.07 examples and case studies

- Representative, edge, failure, historical and cross-domain cases plus context-to-limits structure are excellent. “Representative” needs population/domain evidence; one case should not imply prevalence or generalizability. Realism can conflict with privacy, safety, simplicity and licensing; label synthetic/composite/anonymized examples and avoid re-identification or invented authenticity. Historical cases need source criticism and presentism caution. Cross-domain transfer must state analogy boundaries. Inclusiveness should reflect affected communities without tokenism/stereotypes and use consultation/compensation where warranted. Verify all calculations/code/data, claim citations, dates, permissions, names/trademarks and outcomes independently. Add alternative solutions, failure analysis, uncertainty, ethical consequences, reproducible artifacts, accessibility/localization and criteria for updating contemporary examples. Verdict: **excellent case-design pattern needing representativeness, privacy and anti-overgeneralization safeguards**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.8/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 654–659 — WP-07.08 exercises/solutions/assessment artifacts

- Objective/difficulty/skill/prerequisite/time mapping plus independent solving and learner/instructor trials is exemplary. “As proportionate” could permit skipping every validation path; define minimum author solve plus risk-based independent/learner checks and exception records. Difficulty/time vary by background and accessibility; report ranges and sample. Solvability needs unambiguous assumptions, required tools/data, tolerances, units, randomization and versioned expected outputs. Alternative valid solutions and partial-credit rubrics are important. Restricted materials require role-based access, encryption, leak/rotation plan, academic-integrity policy, privacy and accessibility parity; security must not block disabled learners. Add safety/ethics for experiments, licensing for data/code, generated/parameterized variants, AI/tool-use policy, localization, bias/fairness, solution error corrections and instructor feedback. `[IMPLEMENT/VERIFY]` again blurs author creation with independent validation. Verdict: **exceptionally good assessment QA outline needing minimum validation and secure-access/accessibility balance**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.7/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 660–665 — WP-07.09 visual/tabular content

- This is a comprehensive visual QA package, spanning data accuracy, encoding, captions, attribution, legibility, color independence, descriptions, semantic tables and regenerable sources. Add truthful axis/baseline/truncation, uncertainty/error bars, aggregation, normalization, map projection, image enhancement/manipulation disclosure, scale bars, legends, source-data links and color-vision simulations. Alt text/long descriptions need purpose/context and disabled-reader/manual testing; not every image needs both, decorative items need null alternatives, and complex math/diagrams may require structured/tactile data. Table headers/relationships require actual tagged-output testing after composition. Editable sources can contain proprietary fonts/data and need license/security/privacy. Exports need format/profile, vector/raster, dimensions/DPI, color space, compression and checksums. Localization needs text separation/layout expansion. `[VERIFY]` under author accountability needs independent data/visual/accessibility checks. Verdict: **excellent visual lifecycle specification with data-ethics and final-output semantic validation still implicit**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.8/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 666–670 — WP-07.10 citation/source integrity

- Page-level support, retraction status, persistent identifiers, deduplication and archival alternatives are strong. “Primary-source preference where appropriate” needs a hierarchy by claim: primary studies for results, systematic syntheses for consensus, normative standards/law for obligations, official docs for APIs, scholarly histories for contested interpretation. Existence/relevance/support verification applies to *all* citations, not only automated suggestions; the automation warning is useful but risks implying human-supplied citations are safer. Add source version/date, claim ID/location, directness, quotation context, translations, author/version disambiguation, citation correction propagation, conflict/funding quality, predatory/citation-laundering checks, software/data/model citations and accessed/archived URLs. Web archiving may violate terms or fail for dynamic/private content. Citation counts do not prove completeness. Independent spot/full checks should be risk-based, with no fabricated placeholder references. Verdict: **strong source-integrity rule whose automation warning should become a universal citation-verification requirement**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 671–676 — WP-07.11 front/back matter

- Distinguishing required groups, options and provisional locators is useful, but `[GROUP:ALL] Required as applicable` is logically muddled: ALL means every applicable child, yet applicability/route varies by format/jurisdiction. Title/copyright pages, disclosures, bibliography and author information have different obligations; contributor biographies may be optional/privacy-sensitive. Reader guide and TOC may be inappropriate in some short/reference formats, while accessibility statements, edition/version/as-of date, ISBN/identifiers, license, publisher, contact/corrections, funding/COI/AI disclosures, accessibility features, data/code availability and legal notices may be essential. Epigraphs/forewords require permissions and conflict checks. Index candidates need controlled terms/locators and later professional review. References may be chapter-local. Define source-of-truth generation so TOC/lists/index do not drift, and cross-format front matter order/metadata. Verdict: **useful front/back taxonomy with unresolved applicability logic and several missing modern disclosure/version elements**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 677–681 — WP-07.12 supplementary/companion materials

- Requiring the same rights, accessibility, privacy, security, version, verification, maintenance, preservation and EOL controls as the book is exemplary. Literal parity may be impossible or inappropriate across videos, code, simulations and instructor files; define equivalent outcomes and modality-specific standards. “Option-set” needs selection/rationale, audience/dependency, owner, budget and support life. Add canonical URLs/PIDs, release compatibility matrix, offline/low-bandwidth alternatives, captions/transcripts/audio descriptions, licenses/CITATION, dependency/SBOM, authentication/data collection, analytics consent, moderation, platform/vendor terms, export/migration, backups, integrity checks, uptime/support SLAs and archival snapshots. Solution manuals need restricted access without accessibility loss. Book claims must not depend on an ephemeral website without preserved fallback. Verdict: **excellent lifecycle-parity principle needing modality-specific controls and durable dependency fallbacks**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 682–687 — WP-07.13 multi-author integration

- Voice/term/evidence/accessibility harmonization and explicit contradiction/gap/rights tracking are essential. `{A/E}` as an alternative role is insufficient; volume editor should be accountable, with technical/accessibility specialists verifying relevant domains. Harmonization must not erase legitimate disciplinary, cultural or authorial differences; define house-level invariants versus allowed voice variation. “Remove overlap” can harm intentional reinforcement and cross-path self-containment—classify duplicate, recap and independent reference content. Contradictions may represent real scholarly disagreement and should be surfaced, not forcibly reconciled. Contributor approvals cannot grant veto over corrections/retractions or create indefinite delays; agreements need deadlines/deemed response, due process and editorial authority. Track definitions/claims/citations/artifacts across chapters, versioned integration builds, unavailable/incapacitated authors, credit, moral/rights, replacement transparency, disputes and postpublication responsibility. Verdict: **critical integration package needing single accountability and protection for legitimate pluralism/reinforcement**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 688–693 — WP-07.14 early-chapter developmental edit

- Reviewing a representative completed chapter before scale-up is excellent. “First representative” should mean risk-/coverage-selected rather than chronologically first, and may require multiple slices for heterogeneous books. This duplicates Phase 6 unless the distinction is prototype versus first production chapter; state the delta and reuse evidence. Define editor competence/continuity, artifact/version, rubric, response/disposition, severity, closure and retest. Applying lessons prospectively should also trigger impact review of architecture, prototype, templates and already drafted material; avoid blindly globalizing one chapter’s findings. Reader testing may be needed where the edit reveals audience assumptions. Do not let schedule pressure bypass the hold point. Verdict: **valuable production-scale checkpoint with unclear distinction from the prototype review and overgeneralization risk**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 694–698 — WP-07.15 mid-manuscript integration review

- Midstream review and immediate rebaselining are excellent defenses against late structural failure. “Mid” should be risk/coverage-based, not merely 50% word count; define trigger and integrated artifact. Thesis/outcomes again need alternatives for reference/edited works. Review should include evidence currency, scope/word budget, dependency/definition/notation, duplicated/gap content, cross-references, code/data/visual builds, rights, accessibility, localization, reader paths, schedule/capacity/budget, risk and maintenance. `{E/R}` as alternative cannot cover all domains; assign accountable editor plus independent specialists. Rebaseline needs change request, impact on contracts/prior gates, approvals, reader retest, revised estimates and communication. Include stop/reduce/pivot criteria. Verdict: **high-value anti-deferral review underdefined in trigger, multidisciplinary coverage and prior-gate impact**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 699–703 — WP-07.16 draft tracking/chapter acceptance

- Chapter-level tracking of evidence, permissions, tests, accessibility and defects is excellent. `{A} [MAINTAIN]` should not let authors self-accept quality-critical chapters; separate author-ready status, independent verification, editorial acceptance and gate approval. Use normalized statuses rather than one field, artifact/version hash, acceptance criteria/result, reviewer/approver, open/deferred issues, dependencies and last surveillance date. “Explicitly deferred” must follow Phase 0 owner/date/gate/expiry rules and cannot allow blockers/nonwaivable issues. Chapter acceptance may be revoked by integration, evidence updates or production changes; define reopen/supersede. The loop needs cadence/WIP limits and completion definition for linked artifacts. A dashboard should derive from the missing atomic catalogue, not duplicate it. Verdict: **strong tracking concept with author-accountable acceptance and deferment risks**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 704–715 — Gate 7 manuscript/artifact completion

- The gate wisely requires a complete build, traceable claims/assets, working artifacts, solutions, chapter records, permissions status, integrated review and explicit omissions before independent acceptance. “Completion” overstates maturity because permissions may only have a status, independent acceptance is next, and production/accessibility formats remain unfinished; call it development-complete candidate. “Planned content is present” needs requirement/scope coverage including approved exclusions, not word presence. “Supplements operate” needs clean independent tests, compatibility/version and accessibility. Controlled omissions require rationale, user impact, owner, due gate/date, nonwaivable/blocker check and disclosure. Add zero unresolved blocker criteria, full build/test logs, evidence currency cutoff, rights/license risk, safety/security scan, reader-path/integration checks, reproducible archive, change baseline and known-defect list. The independence rule is weak: a non-author editor/reviewer merely “participates in verification and approval,” may lack domain independence, and one person cannot cover all applicable domains. Require accountable approval plus qualified independent verification coverage. Failure may reopen contracts/gates, not only local work. Verdict: **strong handoff gate mislabeled completion and still permissive on unresolved permissions, omissions and independence**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 716–717 — Phase 8 independent-acceptance scope

- Combining independent verification, peer review, reader/accessibility testing, revision and closure is correct and prevents review from becoming advisory theater. “Independent” does not apply equally to author self-review and internal cross-functional review, so the title should distinguish layered assurance. Define review ordering/parallelism, artifact baseline, issue merge/deduplication and when new evidence reopens earlier checks. Verdict: **excellent assurance phase with heterogeneous independence levels and no review-orchestration model**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.5/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 718–721 — WP-08.01 author self-review

- The checklist is broad and useful, but author self-review is quality control, not independent `[VERIFY]`; label it `[IMPLEMENT/VERIFY]` only if verification explicitly means self-check with later independent acceptance. “Thesis” again needs an organizing-purpose alternative. Familiarity blindness makes self-review weak for gaps, assumptions and reader fit; use a version freeze/rest interval, structured rubric, reverse outlines, claim/dependency reports, aloud/format review and checklists, while documenting limitations. Add code/data/figures/permissions/risks, change history, prior-review response and known issues. Author review must not close independent findings unilaterally. Verdict: **necessary self-check mislabeled verification and naturally incapable of proving several listed qualities**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.3/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 722–726 — WP-08.02 automated/build verification

- The automated surface is impressively broad and the human-interpretation warning is exactly right. “Grammar,” plagiarism/text reuse and citation-hallucination tools produce false positives/negatives and may upload confidential text; require approved local/privacy-safe tools, versions, thresholds, appeal and human contextual review. Automated accessibility scans cannot validate usability/semantics. Citation checks should verify existence, version, relevance and claim support, not only “hallucination.” Equation compilation does not prove mathematics; figure regeneration does not prove truthful encoding; passing code does not prove algorithm claims. Add deterministic clean builds, cross-format validators, cross-reference/index/metadata/alt-text coverage, license/SBOM/security/secrets, reproducibility, broken anchors, source/result diffs, retraction alerts and artifact checksums. Record full logs, environment, coverage, suppressions and unresolved warnings. Verdict: **excellent automation philosophy needing privacy/tool governance and explicit limits for every proxy check**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 727–730 — WP-08.03 independent mathematical verification

- Re-derivation plus symbolic/numerical checks, dimensional/limit/boundary/counterexample and dependency testing is strong. “Central results” needs risk/claim coverage criteria; errors often hide in supporting lemmas, examples and notation. Require verifier qualifications, independence/conflicts, assigned claim IDs, artifact/version, method, full versus sampled scope, assumptions/domains, proof-gap severity, result/dissent and closure. Symbolic/numerical agreement is supportive, not proof, and software needs independent validation/versioning. Include theorem statement consistency, quantifiers/existence, citations to standard results, proof-sketch labels, equality/approximation/error bounds and machine proof where warranted. Multiple specialists may be needed across fields. Verdict: **strong mathematical assurance package without a coverage model or formal reviewer record**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 731–734 — WP-08.04 independent computational verification

- Clean independent execution, platform comparison, dependency/benchmark/tolerance/instruction/archive checks are excellent. Independence requires the verifier not reuse an author-prepared environment blindly; reconstruct from documented artifacts while preserving a forensic copy. Define supported platform matrix, exact versions/hardware, data licenses, seeds/RNG, nondeterminism/statistical criteria, benchmark baselines/methodology, performance variance, numerical precision and expected failure modes. Verify code–excerpt–algorithm–figure correspondence, tests/coverage, security/secrets/SBOM, build provenance, release checksums/signatures and offline archival availability. A successful run does not establish generalizability or security. Record reproduction time/cost, deviations, issues and raw logs. Cloud/hardware claims need calibration/date/job IDs. Verdict: **excellent reproducibility core needing stronger independence reconstruction and statistical/benchmark provenance**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.7/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 735–739 — WP-08.05 independent experimental/statistical verification

- Protocol, calibration, sampling, statistics, provenance, ethics and reporting review is essential. Regenerating results from the same data is computational reproducibility/reanalysis, not independent replication; distinguish audit, reanalysis, reproduction with original apparatus/data and new-data replication. Replication may require new ethics/safety approvals, consent, materials, funding and preregistration and cannot be casually ordered at Phase 8. Define risk criteria, verifier/statistician/domain competence and independence, protocol/version, data integrity/chain of custody, estimands, missingness, multiplicity, uncertainty/effect sizes, sensitivity/robustness, code environment and reporting guideline. Originality alone does not determine replication value. Failed replication needs fair interpretation, author response and no suppression. Protect participant/confidential data. Verdict: **important assurance package conflating regeneration with replication and omitting authorization/resources for new experiments**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 740–743 — WP-08.06 internal cross-functional review

- Cross-functional coverage is commendably broad, but a one-line list does not establish who reviews what, qualifications, independence, conflicts, criteria or evidence. Co-author cross-review is not independent; technical editors cannot substitute for safety/legal/accessibility specialists. “Inclusion/sensitivity” needs defined remit, affected-community engagement, compensation and anti-tokenism. Sustainability/societal impact require methods. Use a coverage matrix by requirement/risk, named accountable integrator, shared baseline, domain reports, contradiction/escalation, issue deduplication, author response, closure and retest. Internal reviewers may face hierarchy/retaliation pressure; provide confidential escalation and recusal. Avoid checklist overload on every low-risk project through tailoring. Verdict: **excellent multidisciplinary intent reduced to an unexecutable role list**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.4/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 744–749 — WP-08.07 external peer review

- Formal selection authority by route, qualification/conflict/confidentiality checks and structured criteria are excellent. CORE external peer review may be disproportionate for internal manuals or low-risk self-published guides; require equivalent independent review based on claim risk/type. Publisher control does not guarantee independence, transparency or adequate coverage, while author-funded self-route reviewers can also be conflicted. Define number/domain coverage, identity model (open/single/double anonymized), compensation, diversity, deadlines, artifact/data/code access, confidentiality/security, AI/tool policy, rubric, raw reports, editorial synthesis, author response, dissent/appeal and review limitations. One reviewer cannot assess every listed science/code/data/safety/audience domain. Originality is not always a goal for textbooks/reference works. Peer review does not certify truth and must not replace reproducibility/accessibility/legal checks. Verdict: **strong peer-review governance outline needing proportionality, multiple-domain coverage and limitations disclosure**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 750–755 — WP-08.08 target-reader/accessibility testing

- Repeating reader tests on the full manuscript is excellent, and the explicit anti-tokenism warning is important. Specialist proxies and AT tests are useful but cannot replace lived experience for claims about disabled-reader usability; say supplement or documented fallback, not equivalence. “Representative novice/intermediate/advanced” is not a sampling frame; recruit by declared pathway, prerequisite, task, language, device/context and disability needs, with rationale/limits. Apply the Phase 6 ethics/privacy/consent/compensation/accommodation controls and prevent participant fatigue. Full-book think-aloud/delayed recall may be infeasible; select risk-based journeys while testing global navigation and cumulative load. Define metrics/rubrics, sample uncertainty, qualitative method, abandonment context, accessibility standards/AT matrix and retest. Do not expose restricted instructor/confidential material. Verdict: **excellent full-manuscript validation commitment with proxy and feasibility caveats requiring explicit ethical methods**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.7/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 756–760 — WP-08.09 feedback analysis/reviewer response

- A complete comment inventory, evidence-based disposition, revision location and disagreement process are excellent. Author accountability alone creates power bias; an editor/review authority should verify that severe comments are fairly classified and resolved. Severity, root cause and affected audience are separate fields; add source/reviewer ID with anonymity protection, requirement/claim/artifact version, theme/duplicate links, owner, due date, rationale, evidence, changed lines, retest, closure authority and communication. “Partly accept” needs exact accepted/rejected components. Reviewer disagreement need not be forced into consensus; preserve reasoned dissent and uncertainty, especially interpretive disputes. Additional review/arbitration must avoid reviewer shopping. Protect confidential reports/personal data and disclose material limitations without deanonymizing. Reviewers may be invited to confirm response but should not bear indefinite approval labor unless agreed/compensated. Verdict: **strong response discipline needing independent disposition oversight and preserved dissent**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.6/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 761–766 — WP-08.10 revision/change-impact/regression control

- The impact inventory is exceptionally good and recognizes that prose edits propagate into code, rights, accessibility, metadata, navigation and supplements. Add requirements/dependency graph queries, contracts/scope/budget/schedule, translations/formats, glossary/notation, safety/security/privacy, claims/evidence currency, version/API, legal/compliance and downstream promotional copy. `[IMPLEMENT/VERIFY]` should separate author change from independent verification. Record change request/rationale, before/after diff, artifact hashes, issue IDs, approver, impact analysis, selected/full regression rationale and results. Testing only revised/dependent material can miss unmodeled effects; require full critical suite/build and output visual/semantic diffs before gate. Reader-facing failures need comparable retest without overfitting. Deletions can orphan references/index/definitions. New findings should reopen affected reviews/gates and surveillance cutoff. Verdict: **excellent change-impact model needing graph-backed traceability and separation of implementation from verification**. **Reader entertainment/readability: 4.7/5.**

### unified-book-process-framework.md lines 767–778 — Gate 8 technical/reader-fit acceptance

- Requiring closed blockers/critical defects, independent verification, reader/accessibility targets, issue closure, regression and explicit residual risk is appropriately stringent. “Major defects … explicitly accepted” needs domain-qualified authority, rationale, reader impact, expiry/remediation and disclosure; legal/accessibility/safety issues may be nonwaivable. “Central results” and “proportionately” require the claim/risk coverage matrix. Reader targets from small samples demonstrate evidence, not universal fit; state uncertainty and unsupported pathways. “Reviewer responses are accepted” is ambiguous—by editor, reviewers, publisher or gate authority—and can create endless reviewer veto. Independence again requires only one non-author technical/review authority, leaving accessibility, safety, statistics and reader fit potentially self-certified; require applicable-domain coverage and segregation. Publisher involvement by route does not guarantee competence/independence.
